And finally: Shea Charles is closing on a move from Southampton to Fulham for a roaring £30m.

Sports.title: José Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013
Sports.content:
José Mourinho has revealed he signed a contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager in 2013 only to tearfully renege on the deal and return to Chelsea.

The football world was rocked when the Scottish great announced he was retiring having overseen a 13th Premier League title triumph during a spell of unrivalled dominance at Old Trafford.

United have failed to return to the top of the English game since Ferguson stepped down, with his successor, David Moyes, sacked after only 10 months in charge.

Mourinho was later brought in, spending two and a half years in charge from 2016, but revealed in a new Netflix documentary about his life that he had agreed to come earlier.

“I go to Chelsea in 2013 but in that period there is something nobody knows,” the Portuguese said in the documentary, which is entitled Mourinho. “I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth, and I think the objective of this work that we are doing is to tell the truth. When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”

Mourinho continued: “I was, of course, very flattered, because Manchester United has an incredible appeal. When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

double quotation mark He phoned me and he was crying. He says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea.’ Sir Alex Ferguson

“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football and, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.”

Ferguson was one of the footballing figures interviewed for the new documentary and admits he was under the illusion Mourinho was accepting the offer, only for the situation to change in a matter of hours.

“Early evening he phoned me and he was crying,” the United great said. “And he says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’ The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

Mourinho had a strong bond with Chelsea after leading them to two Premier League titles, an FA Cup and two League Cups during his first spell.

View image in fullscreen Alex Ferguson’s long spell as Manchester United manager ended in May 2013. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

The Portuguese parked differences with the Chelsea owner, Roman Abramovich, to return to Stamford Bridge after leaving Real Madrid, winning another league crown and League Cup before being sacked in December 2015.

“For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic, but I don’t regret because it was a decision that I made with my heart,” Mourinho, now back in charge of Real Madrid, said.

“And I think it is nature that says something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it’s nature. I did it for love.

“I went back with the feeling of, yes, I go home, but with big responsibility because what I did before is history, and you don’t want to destroy your legacy.”

Sports.title: La Liga president Javier Tebas says ‘Infantino era is over’ at Fifa
Sports.content:
Javier Tebas says Gianni Infantino’s position as Fifa president is untenable, claiming he is “destroying the very essence of football” while calling for reform at the highest levels of the game.

The La Liga president, who is a longstanding and vociferous critic of the current Fifa regime, said “the Infantino era is over” and called for control of the game to be expanded beyond the current “elite”.

While Tebas’s remarks will surprise no one within the game, they maintain the drumbeat of criticism directed against Infantino following his determination to continue in post despite his secret and subsequently quashed plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

In an interview with French newspaper Le Monde, Tebas repeated his call for Infantino to resign, an appeal first made after the World Cup but before the sell-off scandal. “For me, Gianni Infantino’s time has long since passed,” he said.

“I’m not saying this because of recent events; I have noticed this style of management for a long time, though everyone else seems to be discovering it only now.

“Gianni Infantino is not someone who contributes to the growth of football. On the contrary, his projects are destroying the very essence of the sport: the national leagues.

“Football is not limited to the elite. For me, the Infantino era is over. What remains to be seen is when that will take effect and how the succession will unfold. I hope it is not just a matter of swapping out some people for others, but of a genuine overhaul.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino has received the backing of Fifa in spite of Uefa’s threat to boycott all its tournaments. Photograph: Sam Corum/PA

Infantino is battling to stay in post despite an increasingly coordinated attempt by European football officials and others to unseat the 56-year-old Swiss. Uefa has made it clear they regard Infantino’s continued leadership of world football as untenable, the Norwegian FA has called for the president to stand down and a number of European associations have withdrawn letters endorsing Infantino for another term at the head of Fifa.

Uefa confirmed on Saturday that a “departure payment” had been made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary more than a decade ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum after the alleged relationship, allegations Fifa dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

On Saturday night, Fifa published a statement accusing Infantino’s critics of attempting to remove him from office before the presidential election next March. “Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes,” the statement read.

Infantino has also garnered support from prominent nations outside Europe, including the World Cup co-host Mexico and the finalists Argentina. Uefa say a proposed boycott of all Fifa tournaments remains in prospect, with the women’s Under-20 World Cup due to start in Poland on 5 September.

Sports.title: Hibernian stun Rangers at Ibrox while O’Neill misses Høgh treble in Celtic win
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes suffered a damaging home debut as Rangers manager with a 2-1 Premiership defeat to Hibernian compounded by striker Youssef Chermiti being carried off the pitch on a stretcher.

David Gray’s side took the lead in the 12th minute with a Josh Campbell penalty after the video assistant referee (VAR) had flagged up that Vanja Dragojevic, making his first Rangers start after signing from Partizan Belgrade, had fouled Jason Kerr in the area.

There was more woe before the break when Chermiti, subject to a failed bid by Galatasaray for a reported club record fee of £22million, having to go off after picking up an injury.

Rangers pushed forward relentlessly and were rewarded in the 85th minute when the Hibs defender Miguel Chaiwa turned the ball past the goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.

However, in the third minute of added time, the substitute Callum Wright guided a shot into the far corner for a stunning win.

With Celtic and St Mirren both on six points from two games, Rangers are five behind with McInnes looking for his first win after three matches in the Ibrox hot seat.

Kasper Høgh scored a hat-trick, his first goals for Celtic, as the Scottish champions made light of the absence of their manager Martin O’Neill with a 5-1 win at Kilmarnock. O’Neill missed the trip to Rugby Park after what the club had said earlier this week was a “small procedure” in hospital.

No details were given about O’Neill’s operation, which came after the veteran Northern Irish manager took charge of Celtic’s win against Dundee in their first game of the season. But the club’s assistant manager, Shaun Maloney, speaking before Sunday’s kick-off, said O’Neill was on the mend. “He is doing better again,” Maloney told Sky Sports. “He came to the team hotel and spoke to the players but he just needs an extra few days.”

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Kasper Høgh scores the first of his three goals against Kilmarnock. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

O’Neill’s mood would doubtless have been improved by the performance of his side, with Celtic 3-0 ahead before half-time thanks to Høgh. The Danish striker, who joined in July from Bodø/Glimt, needed less than a minute to score his first Celtic goal, heading in at the back post from a cross by Arne Engels.

Høgh doubled Celtic’s lead in the 33rd minute, with Camilo Durán seizing on Johnly Yfeko’s pass out of defence. He combined with Benjamin Nygren to work the ball to Høgh on the left edge of the box, with the forward finishing well.

Two minutes later, Høgh had his hat-trick. Nygren slipping the ball right for Durán, whose cross took the Kilmarnock goalkeeper Max Stryjek out of play, with Høgh nodding into an empty net.

Celtic extended their lead early in the second half after they were effectively gifted a fourth goal by Stryjek. His pass out of defence went straight to Nygren in front of goal and his shot into the top corner made it 4-0.

Michael Schjønning-Larsen pulled a goal back for Kilmarnock in the 56th minute after finishing a well-worked move. But Celtic went four goals ahead again when Luke McCowan, moments after coming on, volleyed in from close range 15 minutes from time after Kilmarnock made a mess of trying to clear the ball from a corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s assistant manager Shaun Maloney took charge with Martin O’Neill still recovering from a procedure in hospital. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

Three Hearts summer signings were on target as Wouter Vrancken belatedly got his reign up and running with a 4-0 win over Dundee United. The Belgian had suffered four consecutive defeats – three in Europe – since replacing Derek McInnes in June, but his new-look team tore United apart in their first home league game of the season.

Tom Renaud, Calvin Miller and Josh McPake all marked their first league outings at Tynecastle with goals, while last season’s talisman Cláudio Braga broke his duck for the campaign.

Hearts made a fast start as Renaud, a few days after notching against Benfica, unleashed a ferocious strike beyond Jack Walton from just short of 30 yards after being teed up by Braga in the fourth minute.

View image in fullscreen Josh McPake turns away after scoring Hearts’ fourth goal against Dundee United. Photograph: Malcolm Mackenzie/Getty Images

The home side were gifted the chance to double their lead when VAR spotted Daniel Bennie wrestling Jamie McCart to the ground in the box. Miller stepped up to fire the penalty straight down the middle.

Hearts killed off any hopes of a United fightback in the 56th minute when Braga drilled in a low angled shot from 12 yards out after being set up by Sabah Kerjota. McPake then marked his first competitive start for Hearts with his first goal as he tucked a clinical low finish beyond Walton after playing a one-two with Braga on the left of the box.

In Sunday’s other 3pm kick-off, Motherwell drew 0-0 at home to Falkirk.

On Saturday, Dundee beat Aberdeen 2-0 thanks to goals from Joe Westley and Joe Bevan while St Mirren edged St Johnstone 1-0 courtesy of Killian Phillips’ penalty.

Sports.title: Iraola says Liverpool have work to do as familiar frailties in defence prove costly
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola told his Liverpool team they have work to do after ­squandering a 2-0 lead against Monaco to lose a second successive pre-season friendly.

The former Bournemouth coach last managed a game at Anfield almost exactly a year ago in the memorable opener to the 2025-26 Premier League season, a game the Cherries were unfortunate to lose 4-2. Now on his debut in the home dugout, Iraola saw his team produce a similarly open display and lose again. It became clear Liverpool’s longstanding defensive frailties are still to be eliminated.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz scored in the first half as the hosts exhibited some free-flowing ­football, but Monaco dominated a ­second half that became fragmented as Iraola and Monaco’s Filipe Luís made wholesale changes.

“As soon as we have made some changes they start to get tired, we cannot sustain that level, so we have work to do,” Iraola told LFCTV on Liverpool’s “frustrating” regression after a bright start. “They were much better in the second half, in the same way we were better in the first half.”

After Liverpool beat Wrexham and Sunderland during a pre-season tour to the US, a 4-2 defeat against Leeds brought back memories of the struggles of last season. This result will cause some concerns with transfer activity dragging.

Ronald Araújo is at least due to arrive on loan from Barcelona. Although that deal is not yet complete and Alexis Mac Allister is still to return from World Cup duty, Iraola’s team to face Monaco was strong, with Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, and Lewis Koumas, 20, the only fringe players to start if you exclude Kostas Tsimikas, back from a loan at Roma. Jérémy Jacquet and Curtis Jones were not considered because of fitness doubts, with Iraola at pains not to “rush” Jaquet, who signed from Rennes for £50m, into action after a chequered time with injury.

Iraola said: “Jérémy, we were in doubt whether to pick him today, he should be fine for the next one. Curtis [there is] something wrong with his hip, [it] didn’t make sense to risk [him].”

Wirtz was sharp, testing Lukas Hradecky with an early shot. Isak’s opener on 16 minutes was met with a hearty cheer from the home faithful, perhaps not surprising given it was just the fourth time the Anfield crowd have been able to celebrate an Isak goal, competitive or otherwise.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola was disappointed after watching Liverpool slip to a second successive friendly defeat. Photograph: Lewis Storey/Danehouse/Getty Images

The strike came after Ryan ­Gravenberch and Dominik ­Szoboszlai’s slick midfield exchange, the former then finding the Swede, who rifled low into the corner. Koumas and Wirtz both squandered presentable chances, but it was soon 2-0 when the German forced home after a ­goalmouth scramble.

Iraola cut a relaxed figure on the touchline throughout and was content with his side’s attacking fluidity. The Spaniard’s preference for a high defensive line was evident throughout, though Alisson was tested far less often than Hradecky until he had to face a 44th-minute penalty after Virgil van Dijk’s trip on Aleksandr Golovin. The Russian stroked home the spot-kick himself to make it 2-1 at the break, giving ­Alisson no chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wataru Endo for Ndukwe and Giorgi Mamardashvili for Alisson were the only half-time substitutions from Iraola, who made more sweeping changes just before the hour, with Rio Ngumoha, Milos Kerkez and the summer signing Víctor Muñoz among those introduced.

By that stage it was 2-2, after Mamardashvili had saved from Mika Biereth only to see the striker tap in the rebound. Monaco’s goals were greeted with eerie silence given there were almost no away fans. There were some groans from home supporters frustrated at seeing their side fritter away a two-goal lead but Ngumoha’s name was sung when he came on.

That Ngumoha was selected on the right wing – Mohamed Salah’s old stomping ground – was lost on nobody, nor was the fact that both the youngster and Muñoz were brought on rather than Federico Chiesa. The Italian did appear after 74 minutes along with Harvey Elliott, who was welcomed warmly back to Anfield after his nightmare on loan at Aston Villa.

Monaco carved out the better chances in the search for the next goal, with Flávio Nazinho firing wide, and Oumar Konaté failing to seize on a good through ball, before their 88th-minute winner stemmed from a corner swung in from the left, which Paris Brunner met with a sweet header.

There was no Anfield roar to push the hosts on to equalise as there would have been in a competitive match, and Liverpool’s side resembled a reserves squad by the end, but it was still a tame finish nonetheless. Only a double-header against Como – the first of which will be played behind closed doors – now remains before Iraola’s competitive debut away at Newcastle on 23 August, with his home league debut coming against Nottingham Forest a week later. The manager will demand an improvement in the next fortnight.

Sports.title: Seesaw draw in Malaysia gives Xabi Alonso food for thought at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Chelsea’s problems mounted as their pre-season tour came to an end in a strangely fiery draw against the Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim. The omens do not look promising with a bloated choice of forwards, echoes of their inexperience and indiscipline last season, and fewer than two weeks for the new manager, Xabi Alonso, to reintegrate key players and work with the entirety of his squad before they kick off the Premier League season against Fulham – managed by his old friend Álvaro Arbeloa – on 24 August.

Alonso, tasked with transforming a club that finished 10th in the Premier League last season into Champions League qualifiers, made 11 changes for the friendly against JDT. He rested players after beating Milan with a strong lineup only 24 hours earlier, 600 miles away.

While the defence and midfield were packed with teenagers, the front three – Estêvão Willian, Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson – would be welcomed by most Premier League clubs, having cost Chelsea more than £100m combined in the past three years.

Delap scored twice from the penalty spot – as many goals in 20 minutes as he managed in the entirety of his first season at Chelsea after joining from Ipswich last summer. The 23-year-old is believed to want to stay and fight for his place, having already proved his Premier League pedigree with 12 top-flight goals for Ipswich. Yet Alonso has so many options: João Pedro, one of the standout strikers last season; the new signing Danny Welbeck; and Jackson, who gave the club something to think about on his loan at Bayern Munich last season.

Emmanuel Emegha arrived recently from sister club Strasbourg, and may well go out on loan. They also still have Marc Guiu on the books.

Mykhailo Mudryk returning unexpectedly early from a drugs ban at the end of July was a curveball, adding to a rich choice of options on the wing including Cole Palmer, Estêvão – looking sharp again on Sunday after an injury that derailed the teenager’s promising first season at Stamford Bridge – and the record signing Morgan Rogers, who frequently played off the left for Aston Villa.

Plenty of time remains before the transfer window closes at the end of the month, but Chelsea’s squad stands at a staggering 41 players, with no European football next season and busy weeks of potential disruption ahead that will not ease Alonso’s stresses.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap scores Chelsea’s second penalty of the evening. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

The JDT manager, Xisco Muñoz, was known for his fierce passion and aggressive football at Watford, and his players treated the game against Chelsea like a competitive fixture at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Johor. They flew into challenges, unsettling Chelsea’s players, competing with an intensity rarely seen in a preseason friendly. The visitors failed to keep tempers in check.

There were several flashpoints throughout the match. Delap and Jackson were needlessly booked for dissent, arguing with the referee about challenges on teammates. Estêvão was lucky not to be sent off after kicking out when he felt he was denied a penalty – instead shown a yellow card.

Geovany Quenda came off the bench and was also booked for launching into an entirely unnecessary challenge, as though settling a score. Sixteen-year-old Reggie Watson was booked in stoppage time, making it five yellow cards.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea received 11 red cards last season – twice as many as any other side and a club record – and Alonso has diverged from the owners’ policy of signing young by adding Welbeck, 35, and Jordan Henderson, 36. The club have not fielded a player over 30 since Thiago Silva, then 39, left in May 2024, but it might take more than a couple of veterans to sort the problem out.

JDT took the lead when they caught Chelsea on a break and Arif Aiman – known in these parts as the ‘Asian Messi’ – scored from a rapid move. Delap levelled just before half-time, then gave Chelsea the lead just after the hour. But JDT equalised three minutes later from Óscar Arribas’s heavily deflected free kick, then retook the lead when Bérgson finished into the bottom corner from distance with four minutes remaining. Mudryk, on in the 87th minute, produced the awkward cross that forced Antonio Glauder’s own goal with a minute on the clock, to avoid an embarrassing defeat.

Chelsea return to London after a punishing schedule. Their last three games were in three countries over five days: Juventus in Hong Kong, Milan in Indonesia and JDT in Malaysia – the last two in successive days, their plane landing in Malaysia at 3am on the day of the game.

Alonso has only two weeks – and one final friendly against Real Sociedad on Saturday – to work with the £117m signing Rogers, the injury-prone captain Reece James and the disgruntled star Enzo Fernández, all due back at the club’s Cobham training ground this week following extended World Cup breaks. Then the season will kick off – and the fun and games will really begin.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Digne returns to PSG from Villa, Fulham agree £30m deal for Charles
Sports.content:
France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris Saint-Germain from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.

The 33-year-old full-back, who featured in six of Les Bleus’ World Cup matches this summer, had two years left on his contract with the Midlands club, with PSG triggering a reported release clause of between £6m-£7m.

Villa confirmed Digne’s exit on their website, adding that he is “a consummate professional, who was highly regarded by his fellow players and staff alike”.

He made 182 appearances in all competitions for Villa, scoring four goals and making 24 assists, after joining from Everton in a £25m deal in January 2022. He played a key role for Unai Emery’s side as they won the Europa League last season.

The Frenchman made 30 Ligue 1 appearances in a three-year spell at PSG until 2016, when he moved on to Barcelona. He told PSG’s website: “I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago.”

Fulham have sought to bolster their midfield by spending £30m on Southampton’s Shea Charles.

Charles, a Northern Ireland international and breakout star of the last Championship season, is expected to sign a five-year deal at Craven Cottage once a medical assessment and legal formalities are completed.

View image in fullscreen Shea Charles was a breakout star in the Championship last season, helping Southampton to reach the playoffs. Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty Images

Fulham will pay an initial fee of £26m, with another £4m dependent on performance, with the size of the fee believed to have ultimately deterred alternative interest from Leeds.

The 22-year-old played 2,000 minutes in the Championship last season as Southampton reached the playoffs before being excluded following revelations of spying against opponents. At Fulham, Charles will be expected to act as the linchpin of the midfield following the sale of Sasa Lukic to Ipswich earlier in the weekend.

Charles joins the young forwards Jonah Kusi-Asare and Gonzalo García as well as 21-year-old attacking midfielder César Palacios on the list of summer signings as Fulham seek to reduce the average age of their squad following the switch of manager from Marco Silva to the former Real Madrid B team coach Álvaro Arbeloa.

Trevoh Chalobah’s move to Como from Chelsea has been confirmed, in a deal worth an initial £25.7m. Terms for a five-year contract were agreed last week, but as the move was announced on Sunday, the England defender said he was “thrilled and honoured” to be joining Cesc Fàbregas’s side.

The pair overlapped at Stamford Bridge towards the end of the Spaniard’s time playing in England, and Chalobah said: “It’s an ambitious, rising project, and working with Cesc Fàbregas again is truly special. I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fàbregas said: “Trevoh is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”

Gustavo Hamer has completed a move from the Championship, this time renewing his relationship with Coventry after leaving Sheffield United for a fee of £6m plus add-ons. The Brazilian-born talent will become the Sky Blues’ sixth signing since returning to the top flight, with two big-ticket deals, £24m goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and £25m Ghanaian international midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi, joining in the last week alone.

View image in fullscreen Trevoh Chalobah will be linking up Cesc Fàbregas after joining Como on a five-year deal Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Hamer was a key part of Mark Robins’s Coventry side as they reached the FA Cup semi-final and Championship playoff final two years ago, only for the attacking midfielder to then leave the club in a £15m deal with the promoted Blades. Following immediate relegation and a misfiring season last term, Hamer will begin a second stint at the CBS Arena, this time under Frank Lampard.

Midfielder Idrissa Gueye has joined Saudi Pro League newcomers Diriyah. The 36-year-old left Everton at the end of last season and arrives at his new club as a free agent. Gueye played in all four of Senegal’s matches at this summer’s World Cup as his country progressed to the last 32.

Elsewhere, Hull completed the signing of the Swedish wing-back Elliot Stroud from Mjallby. The 24-year-old featured in every game for his country at the World Cup and has signed a four-year deal. Reports also continue to link Sporting’s centre-half Ousmane Diomande with a £30m move to Nottingham Forest, with the Ivorian international said to be travelling to the UK from Portugal on Sunday in order to complete his medical. Diomande is understood to be the new Forest manager Oliver Glasner’s first-choice signing, and a player seen as having a key role to play in the German’s preferred 3-4-3 setup.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho made shock U-turn on Manchester United job and broke down in tears to Alex Ferguson
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho made shock U-turn on Manchester United job and broke down in tears to Alex Ferguson

Jose Mourinho tearfully reneged on his decision to replace Alex Ferguson as Manchester United boss due to his love for Chelsea.

The Special One has revealed he signed a contract to take over the legendary Scotsman in 2013 when he stepped down after 27 years of service.

4 Mourinho was lined up to replace Ferguson at United - only for Chelsea to come calling Credit: AFP - Getty

At the time, Mourinho was in charge of Real Madrid, where he would later have his contract ripped up by mutual consent following the Copa del Rey final defeat to Atletico Madrid.

As for United, Ferguson announced his decision to retire on May 8, 2013, with Everton boss David Moyes named as his replacement a day later.

But in a new three-part Mourinho Netflix docuseries which is released on August 11, the iconic Portuguese boss declared he had first dibs.

Though he was left a blubbering mess when informing Ferguson of his decision to shun the chance when beloved club Chelsea came calling - six years after he was sacked at Stamford Bridge.

No way, Jose

Mourinho, who would eventually go on to manage United in 2016, said: "I go to Chelsea in 2013, but in that period there is something nobody knows.

"I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth, and I think the objective of this work that we are doing is to tell the truth.

"When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”

He added: "I was, of course, very flattered, because Manchester United has an incredible appeal.

"When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club.

4 Mourinho was Ferguson's top priority to replace him, with the Special One in tears after going back on his vow

"I think this is more powerful than love for football and, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved."

Are you Fer real?

Ferguson meanwhile recalled: "[Mourinho] was offered a job, yes. I sat him down and explained the situation.

"And as far as I was concerned, he was accepting. And then within hours, it changed.

"Early evening he phoned me and he was crying, and he says, ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’

"The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

Mourinho, who won two Premier League titles, one FA Cup and two League Cups, would bring more silverware back to west London during his second spell.

4 Mourinho won a third Premier League title with Chelsea during his second spell in charge Credit: Getty

Another Premier League and League Cup medal was added to his trophy cabinet, before he was axed two-and-a-half-years later in December 2015.

And Mourinho has insisted he does not regret his decision to initially spurn United, as he stated: "For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic.

"But I don’t regret because it was a decision that I made with my heart.

“And I think it is nature that says something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it’s nature. I did it for love.

“I went back with the feeling of, yes, I go home, but with big responsibility because what I did before is history, and you don’t want to destroy your legacy."

Five months after his Chelsea exit, United were back in for Mourinho, where he this time jumped at the opportunity.

4 Mourinho guided United to Europa League glory in his opening season Credit: getty

In his first season at the Theatre of Dreams, he guided the club to Europa League, League Cup and Community Shield glory, before being axed in December 2018.

And this summer saw Mourinho return to another club in Real Madrid, with club president Florentino Perez whisking him in for a second crack 13 years after his initial departure.

Sports.title: New Premier League club tipped to hijack Liverpool’s move for Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool could be set to face competition from defending Premier League winners Arsenal for the signing of Bradley Barcola.

That is according to talkSPORT's Perry Groves as the Reds push to sign the Paris Saint-Germain winger.



3 Andoni Iraola's Liverpool have been warned their move for Barcola could be hijacked Credit: Getty

Barcola has remained a target for Liverpool throughout the summer transfer window.

talkSPORT revealed last month that an opening bid was set to be placed for the France international.

Although personal terms have not been agreed, Barcola is keen on a move to Anfield.



Liverpool are set to use the fact he has just two years left on his current deal as well as the player's desire to not extend his stay in their negotiations.

Transfer battle

However, Arsenal could now be set to enter the race to sign the 23-year-old, according to former Gunners player Groves.



Speaking on Sunday Session alongisde Sam Ellard, the former Gunners star revealed: "I’ve got a source that says he wants to live in London.

"I can’t tell you (who), I can’t divulge my sources. I’ve got a source. I’ve got a mole."



When pressed on his claim, he simply added: "Barcola wants to live in London."

Groves was then asked which of the two clubs would suit Barcola more, explaining: "I’ve got no dog in the fight, but I would say the Gooners because Liverpool are a team that are in transition.

"Andoni Iraola going in there, imposing his own philosophy, his own style with all the new signings coming in.

3 Barcola would be more suited to Arsenal, according to Groves Credit: Getty



"If you were Barcola and you thought, what out of those two sides have got the most chance of winning the Premier League or Champions League, at the moment you’d say it was Arsenal.

"So it’s whether Arsenal want to go in, if they go in for him, then there would have been advances being made to his people.

"Because they don’t want to be seen losing out on Vinicius Junior being played like a little kitten with a ball of wool, but Arsenal have to be in for those sorts of players. That’s the level Arsenal are at now."

Arsenal's winger search

Arsenal had considered making an attempt to lure Vinicius Jr away from Real Madrid earlier in the window.



Despite their strong position in world football, the Brazil international ultimately penned a new six-year deal with the Spanish giants.

Mikel Arteta's side remain in the market for a new left winger before the transfer window closes, though.

3 Arteta could still look to sign a new left winger before the end of the summer Credit: Getty

It comes amid interest from Turkish champions Galatasaray in Gabriel Martinelli, who could leave if the position is strengthened.



Leandro Trossard has already departed for Besiktas, with Greek Christos Tzolis since arriving from Club Brugge as his replacement.

Sports.title: Premier League club consider shock move for Real Madrid star Endrick
Sports.content:
Aston Villa are considering a loan move for Real Madrid forward Endrick, talkSPORT understands.

Roma are also interested in signing the Brazil international before the transfer window closes.



3 Aston Villa are considering a loan move for Endrick this summer Credit: Getty

Endrick spent the second half of last season on loan at Lyon from the the Spanish giants.

Despite returning to Real Madrid following the World Cup, he could seal another temporary switch away from the Santiago Bernabeu.

The 20-year-old scored eight goals and added eight assists in 21 appearances for Lyon during his loan spell.



Endrick was subsequently part of the Brazil squad in North America, featuring four times for Carlo Ancelotti's side.

A move to Villa Park would bolster Unai Emery's front line ahead of their Champions League campaign.



Last season's fourth place finish in the Premier League means Villa will return to Europe's premier club competition.

They are also set to face Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup on Wednesday as a reward for their Europa League triumph.



Ahead of the new season, Ollie Watkins, Tammy Abraham and Brain Madjo are currently the senior strikers at Emery's disposal.

Watkins finished last term as Villa's top scorer with 21 goals across all competitions.

Meanwhile, Abraham found the net three times following his January arrival from Besiktas.

3 Endrick scored eight goals during a loan spell with Lyon last season Credit: Getty



As for Madjo, the 17-year-old has been the standout performer in pre-season for Villa.

He has already scored four goals for the club this summer and started their latest outing against Bayern Munich on Friday.

Villa transfer plans

Emery has already signed four new players this summer, including the club-record signing of Johan Manzambi from Freiburg.

Midfielder Joao Gomes has also arrived from Wolves along with the loan signing of Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho.



Youngster Modou Keba Cisse has joined the club from Austrian outfit LASK.

There have been notable departures, though, with Morgan Rogers joining Chelsea in a British-record £117million deal.

3 Emery has already landed four new signings this summer Credit: Getty

Villa could still add more players in addition to their interest in Endrick before the window closes on September 1.



A £17million deal for left-back Matteo Ruggeri is close to completion, with the Atletico Madrid defender keen on the move.

Sports.title: ‘Mugged off’ – Rangers booed off as pressure already ramps up on new manager Derek McInnes
Sports.content:
‘Mugged off’ – Rangers booed off as pressure already ramps up on new manager Derek McInnes

Derek McInnes was 'delighted' with the effort of his Rangers players despite their defeat to Hibernian.

However, he admitted his side were hard done by as they fell to a late reverse at Ibrox on Sunday.



4 Rangers can feel 'mugged off' after their loss to Hibernian, claims their manager Credit: PA

Rangers are still chasing their first competitive win under McInnes as they went down 2-1 to Hibs with Gers fans loudly booing once the full-time whistle was blown.

The result leaves Rangers five points off the pace after just two games with rivals and defending Scottish Premiership champions Celtic amassing a maximum six points.

Josh Campbell's controversial penalty had opened the scoring for the visitors after summer signing Vanja Dragojevic was punished for holding Jason Kerr at a corner following a VAR review.



Despite the setback, Rangers appeared to have rescued a point through Miguel Chaiwa's own goal with just five minutes of the 90 remaining.

However, Callum Wright grabbed the winner for Hibs in the third minute of stoppage time with just his side's second shot on target of the match.



To add to Rangers' woes, striker Youssef Chermiti was stretchered off during the first half after colliding with an advertising board.

'Mugged off' - McInnes

Following the match, McInnes said he felt his side were undeserved losers based on the balance of play.



He told Premier Sports: "I thought we were guilty of passing out a few opportunities in the first half and guilty a wee bit of not playing forward enough.

"But I thought going behind to the penalty kick, I've seen it back, I don't think it's a penalty, but we've got a lot of the game to try and rectify that.

"I do think (the penalty) is really, really soft and I'm surprised the referee was brought over to it, but we tried to change one or two things just to try and get more of an attacking threat.

4 Hibernian were controversially awarded a first half penalty by VAR Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



"I thought when we did go into strikers, I thought we were far more effective, and I thought the equaliser was way (less) than we deserved at that time, and I thought we just looked like trying to win the game. I can't afford my players' effort. They went hell for leather to try and win the game.

"I think Hibs had two shots on target, and they've won the game, and it feels as if we've been mugged off a wee bit, and it's a disappointing afternoon. But I'm delighted with the players' efforts."

Rangers registered nine shots on target to their opponents' two during the match.

However, they remain without a victory under McInnes three fixtures into his tenure.



4

4 McInnes is still awaiting his first win as Rangers manager having succumbed to two defeats in three matches Credit: PA

Sunday's defeat follows a draw at Dundee United on the opening weekend and a loss to Jagiellonia Bialystok in the Europa League on Thursday.

Rangers host their Polish opponents in the second leg of their tie on Thursday night.



They then welcome St. Mirren to Ibrox in the second round of the Scottish League Cup on Sunday.

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli could leave Arsenal this summer as European club make shock enquiry
Sports.content:
Gabriel Martinelli could leave Arsenal this summer as European club make shock enquiry

Galatasaray have made an initial enquiry to Arsenal over the potential signing of Gabriel Martinelli, talkSPORT understands.

The two clubs discussed a price for the winger if a deal were to be done this summer.

3 Martinelli has been with Arsenal for seven years Credit: AFP

Martinelli has been identified as a potential target by the Turkish giants after their talks to sign AC Milan's Rafael Leao failed to provide a breakthrough in the deal.

However, any agreement for Martinelli would be reliant on Arsenal signing a replacement.

The Gunners will only sanction an exit if they can sign a left winger of their own.

Several targets have already been identified by the Premier League champions.

Juventus' Kenan Yildiz, Julian Alvarez of Atletico Madrid, Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye and Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi have all been monitored this summer.

Martinelli's future

Martinelli is into the final year of his current Arsenal deal, which expires next summer.

The north London outfit do have the option to extend his contract by a further year, though.

It comes after he signed an extension back in February 2023, four years after joining the club.

Since his arrival from Brazilian club Ituano in 2019, Martinelli has scored 62 goals in 278 appearances across all competitions.

The Brazil international has also provided a further 36 assists in that time.

3 Arsenal would only sanction an exit for Martinelli if another left winger is signed Credit: Getty

As well as winning the Premier League in May, Martinelli has lifted both the FA Cup and Community Shield with Arsenal.

Martinelli featured off the bench in his side's last two friendly outings against Real Betis and Borussia Dortmund.

Galatasaray are not the first club to show interest in the 25-year-old this summer.

talkSPORT previously revealed in June that clubs in Saudi Arabia were also keen on a move for Martinelli.

Their interest came prior to Leandro Trossard's departure to Besiktas.

As for incomings, Arsenal have since replaced Trossard with Greece international Christos Tzolis.

3 Martinelli is into the final year of his Arsenal deal, but the club have the option to extend Credit: AFP

The 24-year-old has joined from Club Brugge on a five-year deal.

Bruno Guimaraes' arrival from Newcastle for £75million was confirmed on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Piero Hincapie has seen his loan from Bayer Leverkusen made permanent ahead of the new season.

Sports.title: Liverpool wonderkid impressed Virgil van Dijk in pre-season and could have solved centre-back crisis – but will be forced on loan
Sports.content:
Liverpool wonderkid impressed Virgil van Dijk in pre-season and could have solved centre-back crisis – but will be forced on loan

Liverpool fans have unearthed a new star in pre-season ahead of the upcoming campaign.

The Reds continued their preparations for the upcoming campaign with a 3-2 defeat against Monaco at Anfield on Sunday.

3 Ifeanyi Ndukwe produced an impressive performance for Liverpool against Monaco Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Despite suffering a 3-2 defeat to the Ligue 1 outfit, there were plenty of positives to take for Andoni Iraola's side.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz were both on the scoresheet during the first half as Liverpool took a 2-0 lead.

However, it was centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe who caught the eye with his display during the opening 45 minutes.

The 18-year-old won three tackles as well as all four of his duels, lining up alongside Virgil van Dijk in central defence.

Ndukwe's tackles and duels won were the most of any player during the first half.

The Austria Under-21 international also completed 23 out of 24 attempted passes.

Meanwhile, one piece of skill in particular earned applause from Van Dijk after his turn left Monaco striker Mika Biereth on the floor.

talkSPORT verdict

talkSPORT's Micky Gray was equally impressed with the teenager's performance, explaining live on talkSPORT: "Played really well in that first 45 minutes, but I think it's because he hasn't played enough international football that they're struggling to get a work permit for him.

"So I think he's going to have to go out on loan.

"We know the problems that Liverpool have got in those centre-half positions.

3 Ndukwe is set to be forced to go on loan despite starring in pre-season for the Reds Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"So that's really unfortunate for him, but I think it's a story that might linger on a little bit."

Following Ibrahima Konate's departure for Real Madrid, Liverpool have just four senior centre-backs at the club.

Of those, Van Dijk is the only one currently fit with youngsters Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet yet to return to action after long-term injuries.

Joe Gomez is also expected to be unavailable until September due to a muscle problem.

However, Liverpool are set to announce the signing of Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona, talkSPORT understands.

3 Van Dijk is currently Liverpool's only fit senior centre-back Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Who is Ifeanyi Ndukwe?

Liverpool agreed a deal to sign Ndukwe from Austria Vienna in January, with the defender joining the club this summer.

His arrival had been delayed until after he turned 18 in March.

Ndukwe was part of the squad which travelled to the USA for the Reds' pre-season tour.

During the trip, he featured in all three matches against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds United.

Liverpool conclude their summer schedule with a pair of friendlies against Como at Anfield on Sunday, August 16.

Meanwhile, at international level, Ndukwe has already been called up to the Under-21 squad.

He was previously part of the Austria side which reached the final of last year's U17 World Cup in Qatar.

Despite that, Ndukwe does not meet the requirements for a UK work permit and will not be able to feature competitively for the Reds this season.

Sports.title: Lucas Digne joins European giants as Aston Villa lose another key player this summer
Sports.content:
Lucas Digne joins European giants as Aston Villa lose another key player this summer

Lucas Digne has left Aston Villa to re-join Paris Saint-Germain, it has been announced.

The French left-back returns to the club he left ten years ago after PSG triggered his release clause in a £6million deal.



5 Digne left PSG to join Barcelona in 2016 but is now back in the French capital Credit: Getty

A verbal agreement was in place last month for the defender who represented France at the World Cup.

PSG in Luc

Upon re-joining PSG, with whom he was at for three years in his first spell, Digne said: "The club has changed, it’s reached another level.

"It’s really incredible to be back here! The Campus? Everything is in place to perform at the very highest level.”



Digne continued: "I can’t wait to see Marquinhos again. We signed for the club at the same time, and now he’s captain and has had an incredible journey, it’s fantastic for him!

"I know Luis Enrique from Barcelona, we had a very good experience together.



"I’m looking forward to seeing my France teammates, but also other people I got to know during my first spell here, such as the kit men. It’s really nice and you quickly feel at home.

“I’m coming back as a man. I’m also a different player. I’ve gained more maturity and experience, and I want to bring that experience to the squad and win lots of trophies.



"This club is built to win, it’s in its DNA. This squad is extremely ambitious, it proves that year after year, and that’s why everyone wants to come and play in Paris.”

Digne isn't the only key player to have left Villa Park this summer with midfielder Youri Tielemans moving to Manchester United in a £35m deal, while forward Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea in a British record deal.

Digne signed for Aston Villa from Everton in 2022, making 182 appearances for the club in all competitions.

5 Digne leaves Villa after four-and-a-half years of service Credit: getty



Last season, he starred for Unai Emery's side, playing 31 times in the Premier League as they secured a top-four finish.

He provided four assists in the top flight, also featuring 11 times in the Europa League as Villa went on to win the competition.

Following the campaign, Digne headed to North America for the World Cup and played six games for France.

The 64-cap defender featured in just one group game, but got more game time as the tournament wore on before France lost to eventual champions Spain in the semi-finals.



His performances attracted interest from French giants PSG, who are set to make him back-up to Nuno Mendes.

Who could replace Digne?

talkSPORT understands that Atletico Madrid star Matteo Ruggeri is the main candidate to replace Digne at Aston Villa.

It is believed that a deal could be struck in the region of £17m for the 24-year-old.

5 Ruggeri could be heading to Villa Park as Digne's replacement Credit: Getty



Ruggeri only made the move to the Wanda Metropolitano from Atalanta last summer, where he featured in 47 games across all competitions.

Villa are yet to agree personal terms with the defender, who is open to a move to a move to Midlands.

Release clause nightmare

Emery would have been planning for the new campaign with Tielemans and Digne in his ranks, however he's lost both for low fees.

Tielemans' shock switch to Manchester United materialised after the Red Devils pulled out of a deal to sign Atalanta's Ederson.



Michael Carrick has been on the lookout for new midfielders, with the Belgian being followed by Andrey Santos from Chelsea through the door.

Villa acted fast to bring in a replacement for Tielemans, as they hijacked Newcastle's move to bring in Johan Manzambi from Hoffenheim.

5 Emery has seen the club sell Digne, Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer Credit: Getty

5 Highly-rated midfielder Manzambi moved to Villa as a replacement for Tielemans Credit: Getty



Manzambi was close to signing for the Magpies, but he hesitated on making a decision, allowing Villa to enter talks.

Villa meanwhile have also sold Rogers to Chelsea in a £117m deal.

And they quickly replaced him with Alejandro Garnacho after snapping up the winger from the Blues on an initial loan deal.

Villa be coming up against Digne and PSG in their first competitive match of the season in the UEFA Super Cup on August 12, live on talkSPORT.

By winning the Europa League last term, they take on the Champions League winner in a battle of the European champions.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho lays into Bernardo Silva's fitness after Real Madrid debut - as he highlights how Man City legend 'doesn't do any work' while on holiday
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho lays into Bernardo Silva's fitness after Real Madrid debut - as he highlights how Man City legend 'doesn't do any work' while on holiday

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has already hit out at Bernardo Silva after his debut for the club.

Mourinho returned to the Bernabeu earlier this summer, 13 years after his first spell, and one of his first targets was Man City legend Bernardo Silva.

The Portuguese midfielder was strongly linked with Barcelona and Atletico Madrid, but Real won the race and Mourinho wanted his captaincy experience and influence to help improve standards and behaviour in the dressing room following a trophyless season that spawned a number of divisive arguments.

After joining up with the squad later due to his participation with Portugal in the World Cup, Silva appeared for the first time in Saturday's pre-season friendly against Ferencvaros, yet Mourinho wasn't happy with what he saw.

'Bernardo Silva?' he said. 'He's a very important player for us. But the poor guy, when he goes on vacation, he likes to disconnect completely, he doesn't do any work.

'So he arrived for pre-season with much lower physical fitness, and he has to improve.'

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho hit out at Bernardo Silva's fitness after his debut for the club

Bernardo featured in Real's 2-1 win over Ferencvaros in pre-season in Budapest on Saturday

Despite his scathing criticism, the legendary Portuguese boss reserved some praise for the midfielder.

'But Bernardo is a wonderful player who gives us excellent build-up with the ball, whether he plays in a deeper position or in midfield (the 6 or 8 position),' he added.

'During the match I saw that he lacks physical strength, so I moved him to the 10 position. He can play there too. He can play in three or four positions.'

Mourinho's side ended up winning the clash 2-1 in what was their fourth pre-season friendly.

They face further matches against Deportivo and Schalke before kicking off the LaLiga season with a trip to Espanyol on August 22.

And Mourinho was happy with where his side were at, although he felt there were still areas for improvement.

He said: 'I liked the first half more. It doesn’t surprise me because we have been working more with those players. We had very good control of the game.

'In the second half, with Vini and Bernardo, who don’t have many minutes, and with Endrick changing positions, we lost some of our organisation. But it’s good.

'You don’t finish the game by giving away a dangerous free kick like we did. You have to know what to do. Those small mistakes that accumulate in these games are good for me.'

Mourinho did praise Bernardo's qualities but added that he has work to do on his fitness

Meanwhile, when departing City at the end of last season, an emotional Silva, who played 460 times for the club and broke down in tears on his final appearance, hailed his 'unbelievable' journey over nine years.

He said: 'It’s difficult because nine years, it’s a very long time. I would say that I leave as a Man City supporter.

'When I arrived from Portugal, I was a fan of Benfica, but now I can say that for sure that my feelings toward this club are very, very strong.

'I will be supporting Man City for the rest of my life. I also have the feeling of being grateful to the club, to the people, to what the fans gave me back. It was just unbelievable.'

Sports.title: Middlesbrough and Tottenham in stand-off over move worth up to £20m for Ashley Phillips after concerns raised in his medical
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough want Tottenham to revise their deal for defender Ashley Phillips amid concerns raised in his medical.

Boro agreed to pay £7million rising to £20m for the 21-year-old centre-back but the deal stalled at the weekend. Though talks are ongoing.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the centre-back was at Middlesbrough's Rockliffe Park training ground last week to complete his deal.

However, issues were raised and the move was put on hold while all parties try to find a suitable solution.

Middlesbrough may now explore an initial loan.

Phillips has spent the past two seasons on loan at Stoke City.

Middlesbrough want Tottenham to revise their deal for defender Ashley Phillips amid concerns raised in his medical

The centre-back originally came through the ranks at Blackburn Rovers and played 14 times for the club until he joined Tottenham for £2m in 2023 at the age of 18.

Despite heading into his fourth season as an official Spurs player, he is yet to make an appearance for their senior team.

Phillips spent the second half of the 2023-24 campaign on loan at Plymouth before his two-year stint with the Potters.

If Middlesbrough are able to revitalise a move, it would continue a busy summer for Kim Hellberg's side.

After receiving a significant sell-on fee from Morgan Rogers' £116m move to Chelsea from Aston Villa, Boro have signed the likes of Jeremy Sarmiento, Will Lankshear, Radek Vitek, Sebastian Berhalter and Kyle Joseph.

They beat Wrexham 1-0 in their first game of the season in the Carabao Cup first round on Friday night.

Sports.title: Phil Foden's girlfriend puts England World Cup tops up for sale on second-hand clothing website - after Man City star was surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel's squad
Sports.content:
Phil Foden's girlfriend puts England World Cup tops up for sale on second-hand clothing website - after Man City star was surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel's squad

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Phil Foden's girlfriend Rebecca Cooke is reportedly trying to sell England World Cup shirts on resale website Vinted.

Man City star Foden was a surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel's squad for this summer's tournament, and it appears that snub also caught his partner by surprise.

According to a report in The Sun, Cooke, 25, is offering the white home and red away strip the Three Lions wore that she appeared to pick up in anticipation of Foden's involvement.

She has priced each kit at £70 on the second-hand website, although they have been slightly modified.

That adaptation was done by a clothing brand which tightened the waist, with the likes of Ellie Watkins, wife of England star Ollie, seen wearing a similar fit out in the US.

The report adds Essex-based company A Vintage Fit altered the shirts to a 'figure-hugging version' for £180.

Phil Foden's girlfriend Rebecca Cooke is reportedly trying to sell England World Cup shirts

Foden missed out on England's squad for the tournament but Cooke is trying to flog the shirts she appeared to pick up in anticipation of his inclusion

She is selling the home and away strips, although both of them have been modified slightly

Cooke is looking to flog both strips - which are 'new with tags' and in size 12-14 - for £70, cheaper than the £89.99 they will cost punters on the England website.

Cooke, who has three children with Foden, is said to have more than 100 items listed on her Vinted page, including four similarly adapted Man City tops.

Her account states: 'Selling new & used authentic items only. Account ran by management team.'

Commenting on her attempted sale of the England kits, a source told The Sun: 'Perhaps Rebecca had one foot on the plane when she got the tops.'

Foden didn't enjoy his best season in 2025-26 as Man City missed out on the title for the second year in a row, yet he still managed 12 goal contributions in the Premier League

Speaking earlier this week during Man City's pre-season tour of the Far East, the attacking midfielder opened up on his World Cup snub.

'I took some time off football, spent some good time with the family, and just rested,' he said.

'Going into this season, I just want to have a really good year, want to try and help the team as much as possible, and try and be one of the leaders, and hopefully win titles as well!'

Sports.title: 'I'm not becoming anyone's meme!': Kyle Walker on righting the wrongs of Burnley's relegation, chats with Vincent Kompany - and adding one more trophy to his CV, 15 years after he last played in the Championship
Sports.content:
It's been 15 years since Kyle Walker last played in the Championship.

Back then, the full-back was yet to win any of his 96 England caps and was worlds away from becoming one of the most decorated players of his generation.

Yet as Walker prepares to return to the level next Sunday, when Burnley kick off their third Championship season in five years at home to West Ham, it is a period he still reflects on fondly.

‘It was a massive part of my career,’ Walker says of his four-month loan spell at QPR under Neil Warnock during the 2010-11 campaign. ‘Playing in the Championship grounds you, but it also teaches you. It can be very humbling as well.

‘Having experienced players like Fitz Hall, Shaun Derry, Clint Hill and Paddy Kenny around me, it was a good dressing room to be in. I fell back in love with football a bit there and it was something I needed to do to make that step up to the Premier League.’

Even though Walker has gone on to win 17 trophies since that spell, the 36-year-old, who earned his first England call-up a month after his time at QPR ended, is as hungry as ever for success after one of the most difficult campaigns of his career.

Kyle Walker is desperate to help Burnley get promoted after last season's relegation

Walker hasn't played in the Championship since a breakout loan spell at QPR in 2010-11

‘It left a sour taste in my mouth,’ Walker says of Burnley’s third successive Premier League relegation. ‘I want to put it right, not just for myself but for the fans who had to deal with it and for the players who have stuck around.

‘I feel we have an obligation to put it right and with the quality we have in the dressing room, we should be getting promoted and going back to the Premier League.’

Having spent much of his career competing for titles, Walker found himself battling the drop last season, a mental challenge he had to get his head around.

Now back in the Championship, a division in which Burnley have hit 100 points in each of their last two seasons, Walker is likely to be part of a dominant team again.

And it is that experience he hopes to put to good use, along with some words of wisdom from a former Manchester City team-mate.

‘I’ve spoken to Vincent Kompany and got advice from him,’ he adds. ‘I asked how he found it (being at Burnley in the Championship) after achieving what he achieved.

‘He said it’s difficult and something that is going to be a task for myself (the expectation to win), but it is also very enjoyable because you become a big fish again, and you get a little bit more of the ball. It's a bit more of the game I was used to playing at Manchester City.

‘Hopefully we can replicate that from when Vinny went up because they broke 100 points and tore the Championship apart.’

Walker, who scored the winning penalty in Burnley's Carabao Cup victory over Notts County on Saturday, is relishing his leadership role at Turf Moor and, despite his age, insists he is still in top physical shape.

Burnley will have a target on their backs from the outset this season, and no player is likely to experience that quite like Walker, with many bright young left wingers keen to get the better of him.

‘I think they try to create, what are they called… memes now,’ he adds. ‘They’ll try and create memes out of me, but I can assure you I am not becoming anyone’s meme.’

Walker sought the advice of his ex-Man City team-mate and Burnley boss Vincent Kompany

Walker said last season's relegation left a 'sour taste' in his mouth and he is determined to 'put it right'

The 36-year-old has been impressed by the early work of new Burnley boss Nicky Hayen

Burnley's hopes of an immediate return to the Premier League have followed another summer of change at Turf Moor, with Belgian boss Nicky Hayen replacing Scott Parker, while first team stars Jaidon Anthony, Maxime Esteve, Florentino and Lesley Ugochukwu have all departed.

And Walker has been impressed by Hayen’s early impact.

‘He's been great,’ Walker says. ‘The information he has given is key and he is very direct. Too much information sometimes kills it, but he has been spot on with his information. He's got his message across really clearly and I'm looking forward to working with him, because I think he's going to be a candidate for manager of the season.’

The Clarets have now been promoted or relegated in five successive seasons, so what advice can Walker pass on to his team-mates to ensure they bounce straight back up again?

‘Success in anything is about mentality,’ he says. ‘Talent gets you so far, but mentality and wanting to do well - not just in big games when it's on TV, or when it's sunny and the fans are there in their thirty thousands cheering your name - it's when it's raining and not on TV, it's 7.45pm on a Tuesday night and the wind's swirling around.

‘That's about rolling your sleeves up, getting dirty, and making sure that we can get the three points.’

Walker’s career hasn’t always been straightforward, on and off the pitch, yet at 36 and 15 years on from that grounding loan spell at QPR, he is content with life and ready to write another chapter in his story.

‘Would I have ever thought that I would experience the things I have in football back when I was at QPR? Hell no. What I've achieved is something I could only have dreamed of.

‘So I definitely am at peace and I’ve achieved a lot, but I'm so hungry for more. Getting Burnley promoted is another trophy I want to add to my collection - I want to put it on my CV.’

Sports.title: Everton and Crystal Palace in advanced talks over Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson swap deal - as Trevoh Chalobah joins Como in £25.7m move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Everton and Palace advance in swap deal talks

Everton and Crystal Palace are advancing in talks over a swap deal involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil.

Initial discussions last week were described as complicated over the difference in value; Johnson, 25, cost £35million from Tottenham when he joined in January and has four years left on contract.

McNeil, 26, was valued at £20m when he saw a move to Palace collapse in January and has one year remaining on contract.

Everton and Crystal Palace are advancing in talks over a swap deal involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil

However, talks between the two clubs are now progressing over a compromise and medicals could take place on Monday.

Johnson has been a long-term target for Everton and David Moyes, dating back to his spell at Nottingham Forest. He joined Palace for a then-club record transfer fee, in the winter window but has struggled badly to find any form and there is a growing sense a move would suit all parties.

McNeil was upset when he failed to get his move away in January but regained his place under Moyes. If all goes well a deal both players could be given permission to undergo medicals early this week.

Meanwhile, Palace are keen to offer a new contract for Jefferson Lerma while Club Brugge are pushing to agree a £10m deal plus sell-on for Pakace's Romain Esse.

Digne returns to PSG

France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris St Germain from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.

The 33-year-old full-back, who featured in six of Les Bleus' World Cup matches, had two years left on his contract with the midlands club, with PSG triggering a release clause.

Digne, who started his professional career with Lille, made 30 Ligue 1 appearances in a three-year spell at PSG until 2016, when he moved on to Barcelona.

France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris St Germain from Aston Villa

He told PSG's website: 'I am very honoured to be returning to Paris St Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago.

'I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years. The working conditions at the Campus are exceptional and reflect the club's ambitions.

'I can't wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team. Once again, I will give my very best to defend the colours of Paris St Germain.'

JAMES DUTTON

Chalobah's Italian Job

Trevoh Chalobah has completed his move from Chelsea to Italian side Como in a deal worth more than £30million.

England defender Chalobah departs Stamford Bridge for an initial £25.7m plus a further £5.1m in potential add-ons, as revealed by Window Watch last week.

The 27-year-old has signed a contract until 2031 with the Serie A club, who are managed by former Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas and are preparing for their first season in the Champions League.

Trevoh Chalobah has completed his move from Chelsea to Italian side Como in a deal worth more than £30million

Chalobah made 151 appearances for the Blues, including 47 last term, after joining the club's academy at under-nine level.

He said: 'I'm thrilled and honoured to be here at Como. It's an ambitious, rising project and working with manager Cesc Fabregas again is truly special.

'I can't wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans. I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together'.

JAMES DUTTON

Sunderland target Ipswich keeper

Sunderland are showing interest in Ipswich Town goalkeeper Alex Palmer.

The 29-year-old has emerged as an option for Regis Le Bris' side as Wrexham continue to push for Sunderland keeper Anthony Patterson who is valued at £8m.

Palmer is also on Wrexham's radar should a deal for Patterson fall down.

Ipswich face Sunderland in the first game of the season.

As well as Palmer, Ipswich have Christian Walton returning from injury and have signed two new Dutch keepers in Kjell Scherpen and Kayne van Oevelen.

The latter may yet go out on loan and Ipswich are among the clubs that have held interest in Newcastle United keeper Nick Pope.

Man City striker in talks with Southampton

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama has agreed to join Southampton on loan for the season.

The former West Ham forward did well on loan at Stoke City last season up until he suffered an ankle ligament injury in January, incurred by a hefty challenge against QPR.

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama has agreed to join Southampton on loan for the season

He has bounced back to full fitness though and has impressed on City's pre-season tour scoring two goals, including a composed finish against Inter Milan, and weighing in with an assist.

The 21-year-old has had interest from a number of Championship clubs including Preston North End, Middlesbrough and Derby County.

Swedish international heads to Hull

Hull City have signed Sweden international Elliot Stroud from Swedish side Mjallby for around £3.5million.

The wing-back has joined on a four-year contract, which includes an option for a an extra year.

The 24-year-old played in all four of Sweden's matches at the World Cup.

West Ham make opening Parrott bid

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott and are exploring a deal for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson.

Parrott, their leading goalscorer last season, started on the bench for Alkmaar's opening league game against Den Haag on Saturday.

The Hammers are prepared to break the Championship record of over £17.5million to get Parrott amid competition from Porto.

Nelson has been on the Hammers' radar before and has attracted interest from Fulham and Benfica in this window.

The 26-year-old had an indifferent campaign on loan at Brentford last season.

The Hammers had been pursuing a loan for Sunderland's Simon Adingra but he picked up an injury and has been wearing a protective boot on his left foot.

United keen on Page

Manchester United are interested in signing Leicester prospect Louis Page.

The 18-year-old midfielder has made 21 appearances for the Foxes and won EFL Apprentice of the Year last season.

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also expressed interest in the England Under-20 international but it is understood he wants to join United.

Louis Page has impressed for Leicester and is on the radar of some top sides

Charles closes on Fulham move

Fulham have agreed a £30million deal with Southampton for midfielder Shea Charles.

The 22-year-old is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours and will sign a five-year contract with the option for an extra year.

Read the full story here.

Willock on Besiktas radar

Newcastle midfielder Joe Willock remains a target for Besiktas.

The Turkish side are working on an offer for the 26-year-old but believe Newcastle's current asking price is too high.

Joe Willock is a target of Turkish side Besiktas this month

Newcastle are continuing to work on a £13m deal for Marseille's Pierre Emile Hojbjerg.

They want an experienced midfielder to work alongside new signings Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba.

Read the latest on Newcastle's summer transfer business here.

Race to sign Tuanzebe heats up

Free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe is attracting interest from Saudi Pro league and Premier League sides.

The 28-year-old centre back had an impressive World Cup on the back of a challenging season with Burnley in the top flight and is ready for a new challenge.

Axel Tuanzebe is drawing a lot of interest from both English sides and abroad

Everton and Brentford have looked at the former Manchester United academy graduate and he has drawn attention from abroad also.

He made 16 appearances and scored one goal last season and spent the two previous seasons with Ipswich Town.

Hamer closes on Cov return

Gus Hamer is due to undergo a medical after Coventry and Sheffield United agreed a £6million deal for the midfielder.

The package for the 29-year-old is worth £6m plus add-ons.

Hamer spent three years at Coventry between 2020 and 2023, becoming a real fans favourite scoring 19 goals in 132 appearances.

Blades manager Chris Wilder hinted last week that Hamer had asked to join Coventry and had already spoken to Frank Lampard. His medical is scheduled for today.
