Sports.title: Verstappen vs Hadjar: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar began his first full season at Red Bull knowing that the last driver in the same position as him lasted just two rounds before being booted out.

That must have been a daunting prospect to contemplate, though it bears pointing out that the senior race team management has changed significantly at Red Bull since Liam Lawson was shown the door after his pair of starts for the team last year.

The more experienced Yuki Tsunoda took Lawson’s place and became the latest in a series of drivers whose reputations took a brutal battering from occupying the garage adjacent to Max Verstappen’s. Tsunoda mustered just 7.2% of Red Bull’s points while alongside Verstappen.

This is the context in which to assess Hadjar’s performance this year. His 8-2 deficit in qualifying is nothing to brag about but he has been much closer to Verstappen over a single flying lap than his predecessors.

Hadjar has done vastly better at collecting points, too, claiming 38% of Red Bull’s score so far. True, compared to Tsunoda he’s had the benefit of a wider field spread between Red Bull and the midfield, but even so he’s already taken more than twice as many points as Tsunoda managed over his 22-race stint at the team last year.

He has achieved this alongside a formidable talent in a car which both drivers have termed “undriveable” on occasions. While the high level Verstappen operates at is so familiar it can almost be taken for granted (his superb second place in Hungary, for example), Hadjar has done a more than respectable job alongside him so far.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Which of Antonelli’s rivals is his biggest threat for the championship this year? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s strong position in the lead of the championship standings at the summer break is remarkable enough already for a driver in his second season in Formula 1.

But what makes his position all the more impressive is that, arguably, no single driver has yet emerged as his clear rival. Antonelli has won six of the 11 rounds so far, more than the rest put together, and only his team mate George Russell has taken multiple wins.

Despite that, Russell is not Antonelli’s closest rival in the standings: Lewis Hamilton is leading a resurgent Ferrari. Plus, the final round before the summer break saw McLaren claim their first victory of the season. Three of the last five grands prix were won by teams other than Mercedes – could Antonelli biggest threat come from one of them?

Lewis Hamilton

50 points behind

The possibility of Hamilton fighting for the championship against the driver who took the Mercedes seat he vacated last year is a compelling narrative. But is it a likely outcome? Hamilton is Antonelli’s closest rival in the points but has missed opportunities due to penalties in recent races.

George Russell

59 points behind

Russell should be Antonelli’s closest rival for the championship but various factors have left him well behind including unreliability (not that Antonelli has been immune), some misfortune and his risky first-lap lunge at Spa. He’s also on course to incur a power unit change penalty before his team mate. Still, Russell should have the equipment and the experience to put Antonelli under pressure.

Charles Leclerc

81 points behind

Hamilton may be closer to Antonelli in the standings but Charles Leclerc has arguably looked more competitive. Providing he avoids a repeat of the dip he fell into around Spain and Monaco, he could emerge as Antonelli’s biggest threat.

Lando Norris

91 points behind

Like Mercedes, unreliability has dogged McLaren this year. They often haven’t been quick enough either, though Norris has now won both a grand prix and a sprint race. The MCL40’s Hungaroring upgrade clearly paid off, and may prove enough to bring the McLarens into regular contention. The reigning world champion is a long way behind, though.

Max Verstappen

110 points behind

If last year demonstrated anything, it is unwise to write off Max Verstappen if he is not mathematically out of contention. Having been 104 points off the lead with 249 remaining, he eventually lost by the narrowest margin in F1 history (relatively). But lying 110 points behind in a car which hasn’t won a grand prix yet may be too much even for him.

Oscar Piastri

127 points behind

Oscar Piastri has proved a close match on pace for his team mate as usual but he’s even further behind in the standings. He went into the final round of last season with a shot at the championship but that doesn’t look likely to happen this year.

Isack Hadjar

151 points behind

Isack Hadjar has impressed with the quality of his performances alongside Verstappen and may yet recover the points he dropped after losing his podium finish in Monaco. But his points deficit to Antonelli is surely too large and the Red Bull not competitive enough yet for him to be a realistic title contender.

I say

Hamilton may be closest in the points but Russell surely has the better combination of opportunity and equipment at the moment. If he can stop the rot in the second half of the season I would back him to put Antonelli under pressure for the title.

Sports.title: Domenicali resists Briatore’s call for sprint races at every round | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali will not move to add sprint races at every round next season, but still plans to hold more than the current six.

Alpine consultant Flavio Briatore recently argued for F1 to hold sprint races every week and, as is done in Moto GP.

Speaking in Liberty Media’s latest earnings update call for investors, Domenicali said limiting the number of sprint rounds gives them scarcity value.

“Sprint races is an opportunity that, first of all, started because we wanted to produce something that could create action on the track, creating leverage for the promoter and ourselves to create action on the tracks starting for the weekend,” he said. “We’re going to have more sprint races next year, yes. We’ll inform when we will announce the calendar, how many.

“The principle is very simple. This is also an opportunity to increment the revenue stream, for sure. This is an opportunity for us to have new deals, as we have already seen, and moving in this direction will be our future. We want to do in the right way because, of course, this will allow us also to make sure that the scarcity is a value.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says he ‘let pressure destroy me’ in mid-season slump last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he succumbed to pressure when he suffered a slump in form during the middle of his debut season last year.

The Mercedes driver went through a seven-round spell when he finished in the points just once – albeit on the podium. His dip in form coincided with changes to Mercedes’ car which he struggled to get to grips with.

“I had a good start to the season, then I had a difficult period,” said Antonelli in a recent interview. “In the European season I really struggled and in that moment I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period.

“I felt like I was letting down so many people who had believed in me. Of course especially Toto [Wolff, Mercedes team principal], because he was the main one who took the decision [to promote him].

“Obviously I didn’t feel good in that period. I wasn’t doing well. But then I had a big meeting with the team after the European season and it kind of allowed me to reset and just start again.

“Then I slowly found my way back. I had a good second half of the season and that gave me confidence, being able to overcome those difficult moments and gave me the confidence ahead of this year. It also made me learn a lot about myself, not only as a driver, but as a person as well.”

Antonelli said the experience taught him useful lessons about coping with adversity. “Obviously [during] that European season, I think probably most of the things I did, didn’t help me at all,” he said.

“But also I learned about how my body responds to those moments, how my brain responds, what helps me to get back into the right focus, the right mindset, what helps me to stay 100% in terms of energy during the whole weekend. So how to manage myself with events, obviously the driving and everything. So I’ve learned a lot about myself and how as well to respond to difficult moments.”

Mercedes promoted Antonelli directly to their top team, in the seat formerly occupied by Lewis Hamilton, at the age of 18. Antonelli said making his F1 debut with a front-running team left him feeling depleted by the end of the 24-round championship.

“I was so drained at the end of the year,” he said. “Obviously the team did an incredible job in trying to protect me. But the learning curve – I think I’ve learned much more than if I would have done in a smaller team.

“The learning curve was incredible, it was like doing three years at once. It was overwhelming, physically, mentally, because I’ve made so many new experiences as well.

“Also, doing a full F1 season for the first time, you don’t really know where you’re going, what you’re about to face. Obviously the year prior to F1, I’ve been doing race shadowing and everything, but it’s not the same.

“When I was doing shadowing, I was watching, I wasn’t there on track doing the job. So I felt very overwhelmed at the end of the year. And it was good to have a bit of a break to just have a little bit of time to analyse and reflect on the year and understand what were the good things and why and why some things went not in the right way.”

Having become the youngest driver to lead the world championship, Antonelli says he is trying to enjoy the position and the attention which comes with it, particularly in his home country.

“It’s like in any sport at the highest level, there’s always pressure and of course, being Italian, Italy has been missing an Italian driver for quite a long time and obviously also knowing myself because I’m Italian.

“We know how as Italians we can get very excited about things and how expectations can get over the moon. But obviously that comes with a bit of a extra pressure. But I’ve been enjoying, I have been enjoying. I think what I’ve been trying to do as well is to embrace the pressure and trying to actually shine under pressure.”

Sports.title: Norris vs Piastri: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The super-close contest between the McLaren team mates last year would have made for a thrilling world championship fight even if Max Verstappen hadn’t got involved.

Now in their fourth season as team mates, with a completely different type of McLaren to get used to, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been fairly well-matched on the whole. However in individual races their relative performance has varied, most notably in Hungary last weekend, where Norris was clearly much quicker.

Norris has been on a strong run lately, out-qualifying his team mate for the last five rounds in a row. Though it bears pointing out that Piastri missed first practice at the last round and was badly baulked by Lewis Hamilton when he began his final run.

It took Piastri until the third round of the season merely to start a grand prix, suffering a mortifying pre-race crash at home, then retiring before the start along with Norris in Shanghai. He rebounded magnificently at Suzuka and might have won had it not been for the timing of a Safety Car period.

McLaren have had further technical trouble since then: Norris had back-to-back failures while Piastri’s retirement in Hungary capped a frustrating race where a wayward backmarker had already cost him the lead. Piastri had a rough race in Canada as well, where both McLaren drivers paid the price for a tactical gamble which backfired.

It was therefore fitting that Norris delivered the team’s first win as F1 headed into the summer break. His 36-point lead over Piastri looks like a fair reflection of their relative performances given the various setbacks both drivers have suffered. The world champion holds the upper hand so far but Piastri is keeping him honest as always.

Sports.title: Errol Spence’s Decline Started Years Before Crawford
Sports.content:
“It was quite sad watching Errol Spence in that fight, to be honest with you,” Hearn said to Jai McAllister Boxing. “Having promoted him in his prime in the Kell Brook fight, like how good he was. He was a shell of himself, and I think he has been for years.”

Spence had been putting considerable strain on his body well before his October 2019 car crash. He allowed his weight to climb substantially between fights and acknowledged having to spend portions of training camp taking it back off. After his grueling win over Shawn Porter in September 2019, Spence admitted there was nothing good about gaining more than 25 pounds and then using camp to lose it. The crash came less than two weeks later and kept him out of the ring for more than a year.

Spence returned against Danny Garcia in December 2020 and won comfortably, but the destructive version that finished Brook wasn’t there. Garcia was 32 and already had losses to Porter and Keith Thurman.

The difficulties continued against Yordenis Ugas in 2022. Ugas badly hurt Spence in the sixth round before Spence recovered, took control, and ended the fight in the tenth.

Crawford then produced the most one-sided defeat of Spence’s career in July 2023, dropping him three times before the ninth-round stoppage.

The performance deserves full credit. But it also created the impression that Crawford alone was responsible for making Spence look so ordinary.

Years of difficult weight management, punishing fights, inactivity, and the physical consequences of the car crash had already taken something from Spence before Crawford got him.

Hearn saw Spence near his best against Brook. His belief that Spence had been a shell for years supports what the previous fights were already showing: Crawford didn’t destroy the prime version of Errol Spence.

Sports.title: Car Salesman Hearn Over-Sells Teremoana’s Heavyweight Future
Sports.content:
“I don’t think you guys have seen anything like this before in Australia,” Hearn said. “I think legitimately a chance for you to have a long-reigning heavyweight world champion. Got the size, got the power, got the personality.”

The physical tools are obvious. Teremoana is 11-0 with 11 knockouts, has enormous size and power, and reached the quarterfinals at the 2024 Olympics. What he doesn’t have is a professional win that supports Hearn’s enormous expectations.

Calling DeAndre Savage a “big step up” only inflates Wednesday’s fight. Savage is 35 with a 10-1 record, and Brandon Moore beat him over 10 rounds last year. He’s a reasonable opponent, but beating him tells us little about Teremoana’s ability to compete with the best heavyweights.

Hearn went further, saying he sees “something different” in Teremoana and believes he can bring heavyweight world titles to Australia.

Harrison couldn’t resist.

“You made Teremoana sound like he’s fighting Hercules,” Harrison told Hearn during an exchange in which he joked about the promoter’s ability to sell fighters.

That’s the issue. Teremoana may eventually justify Hearn’s praise, but blasting through lower-level heavyweights doesn’t establish that he’s destined for a long championship reign.

We still need to see him fight beyond the early rounds, deal with a skilled heavyweight who can neutralize his pressure and make adjustments when raw power doesn’t immediately solve the problem.

If Hearn really has Australia’s next elite heavyweight champion, give Teremoana opposition that lets him prove it.

Sports.title: How Wealth and Fame Changed Jack Dempsey
Sports.content:
Everything changed after Dempsey destroyed Jess Willard on July 4, 1919. The heavyweight championship turned Dempsey into one of America’s biggest sports celebrities. His fights generated enormous gates. Movies and endorsements brought him even more money. He also became part of Hollywood’s social world.

The fighter who once struggled financially could now afford mansions and a lifestyle that would have been unimaginable during his early years. Boxing gradually occupied less of his time.

After defeating Georges Carpentier in July 1921, Dempsey went nearly two years without defending his championship. He returned to beat Tommy Gibbons in July 1923 before surviving a wild fight with Luis Ángel Firpo two months later.

Dempsey was only 28 after stopping Firpo, an age when a heavyweight champion might normally be approaching his best years. Instead, he didn’t have another official fight for nearly three years.

During that period, Dempsey’s celebrity continued growing. Hollywood remained part of his life; he participated in exhibitions, and in 1925 he married actress Estelle Taylor. His relationship with longtime manager Jack “Doc” Kearns also ended bitterly.

The contrast with the hungry fighter who had pursued Willard was striking. Dempsey no longer needed to fight regularly to make money or establish his name. Boxing had already given him financial security and national fame.

When Dempsey finally returned to defend against Gene Tunney on September 23, 1926, he was 31 and hadn’t competed in an official bout since Firpo.

Tunney took advantage, outboxing Dempsey over 10 rounds to win a unanimous decision and the heavyweight championship. The inactivity shouldn’t be used to diminish Tunney’s accomplishment. Tunney was an exceptional fighter who defeated Dempsey again in their famous 1927 “Long Count” rematch.

But the larger question remains: what might Dempsey’s career have looked like if wealth and celebrity hadn’t pulled him so far from regular competition? Dempsey became champion at 24. By his late twenties, he had money, mansions, movie work, and access to a world far removed from the one that created the Manassa Mauler.

Success didn’t destroy Jack Dempsey. It gave him the life he had fought to obtain. The price was that boxing no longer demanded everything from him.

Sports.title: Tamm Thibeault Can’t Afford To Wait For Claressa Shields
Sports.content:
She captured the IBF and WBO middleweight titles Saturday night with a 10-round shutout of Desley Robinson, winning 100-90 on all three scorecards. It was her first time going 10 rounds, and she had to deal with a cut caused by an accidental head clash.

Gaining extra ring time would help, but there comes a point where waiting becomes counterproductive. If Thibeault spends another two or three years building her record against lower-tier middleweights, she will be 31 or 32 before getting Shields.

Who is she supposed to fight in that period that prepares her for Claressa?

There isn’t another Shields available at middleweight. Thibeault can collect defenses and complete rounds, but opponents at levels below Shields aren’t going to duplicate her hand speed, reflexes, or ability to make adjustments.

Shields hasn’t exactly been sharpening herself against elite opposition, either. Savannah Marshall in 2022 was the last opponent who presented her with the kind of threat Thibeault potentially brings. Shields has continued collecting titles since then without facing someone capable of seriously testing her.

That doesn’t make Thibeault the favorite. Shields remains the more accomplished professional and has dominated everyone put in front of her.

Thibeault’s best opportunity may come sooner rather than later. She possesses the amateur schooling, size, southpaw stance, and physical strength to make the fight interesting.

Waiting years for preparation that lesser opposition cannot provide may leave Thibeault older without making her any more ready for Shields.

Sports.title: Stopping Hrgovic Would Top Joshua’s Charles Martin Blitz
Sports.content:
He had won the vacant belt less than three months earlier when Vyacheslav Glazkov suffered a knee injury and was unable to continue in the third round. Martin never had to beat a reigning champion to get the belt, then surrendered it in his first defense against Joshua.

Hrgovic is a much tougher proposition. Gareth A. Davies believes a stoppage win would make Itauma’s first title victory more impressive than Joshua’s demolition of Martin.

“I’d like to see a stoppage of Filip Hrgovic, but if you want the major statement, that’s it. And he’s a world champion, and he’s got a stoppage. And if you compare it to Anthony Joshua winning against Charles Martin, winning the IBF title against Charles Martin, then, you know, it does have comparative values, and it’s probably a bigger performance, and it’s probably a bigger statement than that could ever have been,” said Gareth to talkSPORT Boxing.

Hrgovic has already shared the ring with Daniel Dubois, Zhilei Zhang and Joe Joyce. He is durable, physically strong and willing to trade when opponents come after him.

Itauma hasn’t faced anyone close to that level yet. Jermaine Franklin, Dillian Whyte and the other heavyweights on his record haven’t forced him through the kind of fight Hrgovic can potentially provide.

If Itauma runs through Hrgovic anyway, the belt will only tell part of the story. Joshua flattened Martin, but Itauma would have stopped the better heavyweight.

Sports.title: Catterall Could Jeopardize Haney’s Ryan Garcia Payday
Sports.content:
That could take away one of Devin’s useful tactics.

Haney repeatedly clinched Brian Norman Jr. to shut down his offense during their bout. Catterall isn’t a fighter who can necessarily be controlled that way. He uses plenty of holding himself and has the strength to handle Devin in those physical exchanges.

The larger concern is what a loss would do to Haney’s future. A lucrative Garcia rematch would likely remain marketable if Catterall pulled off the upset, but Haney’s bargaining power could take an immediate hit. Losing his WBO belt before facing Garcia could weaken his leverage when the purse split is negotiated.

It could also delay the rematch.

If Catterall beats Haney, there would be considerable pressure on Devin to avenge the defeat rather than immediately move on to Garcia. Another training camp and dangerous fight would stand between Haney and the massive payday he wants, with a second loss to Catterall potentially doing serious damage to his career.

Amino Boxing believes Catterall has been smart to avoid getting dragged into Bill Haney’s social-media battles.

“Jack a smart dude. When you responding to Bill you already lost. Jack staying ahead of the bullshit. Not letting them control the narrative and destroy his reputation.”

Catterall did what he needed to do by publicly stating that he accepted the fight. “Accepted the fight and heard nothing since,” he said on X.

Now the decision rests with Team Haney. If they go elsewhere, the business logic isn’t difficult to understand. Catterall offers Devin considerable danger without providing the payday that makes taking the risk easier to justify.

Sports.title: Top Rank Faces Big Call On Abdullah Mason Against William Zepeda
Sports.content:
“That would be a career-defining fight for me at this point,” Mason said on The Porterway Podcast. “He has everything that somebody would wanna see me face. He’s strong on the front foot, a volume puncher, he’s using his head. It would definitely be a step up from any fight that I ever had before.”

Mason is correct about the step up. Zepeda presents an extreme version of the style that caused him trouble against Sam Noakes last November.

Noakes out-slugged Mason during stretches of their fight and applied constant pressure, forcing the younger fighter to get on his bike and box from the outside during the championship rounds. Mason won the decision to take the vacant WBO title, but it was a grueling night.

His first defense against Albert Bell on July 4 brought another difficult test. Bell fought Mason to a standstill through six rounds before Mason began roughing him up inside to gain control. Mason eventually dropped and stopped Bell in the 12th.

Zepeda would bring considerably more pressure than either opponent.

The 30-year-old threw 884 punches against Roach, landing 218. He has the chin to stay in front of opponents, throws combinations almost continuously, and gives them little time to set their feet.

That could be particularly uncomfortable for Mason, who likes loading up on uppercuts and other power shots. His punch resistance has also shown vulnerability. Yohan Vasquez dropped Mason twice in their 2024 fight before Mason recovered to score a second-round knockout.

Zepeda isn’t likely to disappear after landing one big shot, either. He’ll keep coming, forcing Mason to fight at a pace and under sustained pressure that he hasn’t dealt with as a professional.

“The Sam Noakes fight was a crazy fight, an amazing fight,” Mason said. “I’ve grown from all my past fights, so me being able to implement everything that I’ve learned, it will show where I’m at in the sport facing Zepeda, who’s coming off a great win.”

Mason clearly wants to find out where he is. Top Rank must decide if it wants the answer this soon.

Sports.title: “Bodybuilder Boxer”: Thurman Unsure If Benn Has The Skill To Beat Garcia
Sports.content:
“Yeah, it’s interesting. I still don’t know what to think too much about Conor Benn. You know, he reminds me of like just those guys at the gym that are a little bit like bodybuilder boxers. You know, like they’re just shredded. They train hard, they got the physique, and they’re rough and tough, but where exactly is his IQ? Where’s the skills? Where’s the technique?” Thurman told Fight Hub TV.

Garcia gives Benn an opportunity to answer those questions. Benn can apply relentless pressure, throw with power and force grueling exchanges, but Ryan possesses the faster hands and sharp counterpunching to punish aggressive entries.

Thurman isn’t dismissing Benn’s chances. He compared that raw style to dealing with a charging rhino, pointing out that pure force remains dangerous regardless of technical shortcomings.

“It’s not that it’s a guaranteed loss for a fighter of that type of caliber. It’s not a guaranteed loss, but at the highest level, you will run into skillful opposition,” Thurman said.

Ryan provides exactly that test.

Benn’s pressure gives him a route to making Garcia uncomfortable, particularly if he can trap the champion on the inside rather than allowing Ryan to operate at his preferred range. The danger comes while crossing that distance, where Garcia’s speed and counterpunching can make Benn pay for reckless attacks.

Thurman’s criticism places the burden on Benn to show that there is more to his game than pure athleticism when he meets Garcia.

Ghana News.title: T.I. Ahmadiyya SHS, Salaga book Savannah region’s only NSMQ ticket for second consecutive time
Ghana News.content:
‎T.I. Ahmadiyya Senior High School, Salaga has secured the Savannah Region’s only ticket to the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) National Championship after seeing off Bole Senior High School and Salaga Senior High School.

‎

‎The school finished the contest with 31 points, beating Bole SHS, which placed second with 26 points, while Salaga SHS ended the contest with 4 points.

‎

‎The victory marks T.I. Ahmadiyya SHS, Salaga’s second consecutive qualification for the national championship, keeping the school’s impressive run in the competition alive.

‎

‎Bole SHS came close to claiming the region’s sole ticket but could not overcome T.I. Ahmadiyya SHS, Salaga in the decisive stages of the contest, bringing their hopes of returning to the national stage to an end.

‎

‎For Salaga SHS, the contest also ended in disappointment as the school’s hopes of securing a place at the national championship were dashed.

‎

‎With the qualification secured, the T.I. Ahmadiyya SHS, Salaga team has vowed to build on its regional success and continue its dominance as it heads to the national stage.

‎

‎The school will now represent the Savannah Region at the 2026 NSMQ National Championship, with the team determined to raise the flag of the region high when the national contest begins.

Ghana News.title: Economic recovery must improve lives, not just statistics — Gideon Boako
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako

The Member of Parliament for Tano North and Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako, has said Ghana’s economic recovery cannot be considered complete unless improvements in macroeconomic indicators translate into better living conditions for ordinary citizens.

Dr Boako said economic performance should ultimately be judged by the experiences of unemployed graduates, traders, farmers, contractors and households rather than solely by figures such as inflation, fiscal balances and economic growth.

He argued that citizens are more concerned about access to jobs, functioning businesses, good roads and the ability to meet their daily needs than positive statistics presented in government reports.

“Ultimately, citizens do not vote for economic statistics. They vote for better lives,” he said. Dr Boako added that the real verdict on the economy would be determined by “the unemployed graduate searching for work, the trader trying to keep her business alive, the contractor waiting to be paid, the farmer transporting produce over poor roads and every Ghanaian family still waiting for the promise of economic recovery to arrive at their doorstep.”

He said Ghana needed to move beyond headline economic improvements towards broad-based and inclusive growth that creates opportunities and raises living standards.

According to him, sustainable economic stability should provide the foundation for stronger productivity, employment and improved livelihoods rather than become an achievement in itself.

“Until that happens, growth without visible progress will remain an incomplete success,” Dr Boako said, stressing that Ghana could not achieve broad-based, shared and inclusive growth without strong and sustainable economic stability.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t cannot claim fiscal prudence by cancelling development projects — Gideon Boako
Ghana News.content:
The Tano North MP and Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako, has questioned the government’s fiscal strategy, arguing that reduced public expenditure should not be celebrated as fiscal discipline when it results in the cancellation or postponement of development projects.

Dr Boako said while the government has highlighted improvements in its fiscal position, the reported underspending against amounts approved by Parliament raises concerns about whether the gains reflect greater efficiency or simply a failure to implement planned projects.

He cited an International Monetary Fund report which, according to him, indicates that about 1,800 ongoing projects had been cancelled and roughly 2,000 others rephased.

He said the affected projects included roads, drainage systems, schools, hospitals, teacher and health-worker accommodation, agricultural warehouses and electricity infrastructure, all of which have direct implications for communities and households.

“Is the government genuinely becoming more efficient, or are projects simply not being implemented as planned?” Dr Boako asked, arguing that the government should not sacrifice development expenditure merely to achieve favourable fiscal indicators.

He compared the approach to a household that improves its finances by postponing essential repairs and obligations.

“A family can appear financially healthy by postponing roof repairs, delaying children's school needs or refusing to fix a leaking pipe. The monthly budget may look impressive, but the underlying problems continue to grow,” he said.

Dr Boako maintained that genuine fiscal prudence must strike a balance between controlling expenditure and investing in projects that expand economic opportunities and improve living standards.

“Fiscal discipline should never become an excuse for development paralysis,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Growth without jobs is growth without hope — Gideon Boako
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako

The Member of Parliament for Tano North and Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako, has criticised what he describes as an excessive focus on macroeconomic indicators, arguing that economic growth must ultimately translate into jobs, higher incomes and improved living standards.

According to him, the greatest test of the government’s economic policies is whether young people can secure decent employment and whether businesses, farmers and households are experiencing meaningful improvements.

He said a young graduate would gain little from lower inflation or a reduced fiscal deficit if there was no job available after completing university.

“A young graduate does not celebrate a lower fiscal deficit if there is no job waiting after university. A farmer does not benefit from higher GDP figures if poor roads continue to prevent produce from reaching markets,” he said.

Dr Boako also argued that traders and businesses judge the economy by the purchasing power of consumers, access to credit and the ability to sustain operations, rather than by fiscal indicators alone. He said contractors waiting to be paid and farmers struggling with poor roads similarly feel little benefit from fiscal surpluses that do not translate into actual economic activity.

He said Ghana had achieved periods of macroeconomic stability in the past. Still, the country’s recurring economic challenges showed that stability must be converted into productive investment, industrialisation, employment and rising incomes.

“Macroeconomic stability should never become the final destination. It should be the platform from which governments build prosperity,” he said.

Dr Boako said the real measure of the current recovery would therefore be whether factories expand production, agriculture becomes more productive, exports diversify, infrastructure improves and young Ghanaians find meaningful employment.

“That is the transformation Ghanaians are still waiting for,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Nii Lantey Vanderpuye confident of winning NDC chairmanship
Ghana News.content:
Former National Coordinator of the District Road Improvement Programme (DRIP), Edwin Nii Lantey Vanderpuye, says he is confident of winning the National Chairmanship of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

Mr Vanderpuye said his confidence stems from his longstanding commitment to the NDC and years of service to the party.

The former MP and minister described himself as a foundation member of the NDC, saying he had served at various levels, from the grassroots to Parliament, government and the presidency.

“At every time I go on my knees to pray, there is that joy that comes into me, and that gives me the sense of victory. I am sure I’m going to win the NDC chairmanship, no matter what,” he said on WoezorTV on Sunday, August 9, 2026,

Mr Vanderpuye said his decision to contest was motivated by a desire to give back to the party, which he credited with providing him opportunities to serve the country.

He said his decades of involvement in the NDC had sometimes come at the expense of his family but maintained that his commitment to the party remained a lifelong responsibility.

“I’ve done more work in this party than many. I don’t know how many people I can count that have been involved in the development of the party, in the progress of the party, more than me,” he said.

“I think it is time for me to crystallise all those things I’ve done in the background by sitting in a chair now and making sure that the vision we share as a family, the NDC, is articulated the way it should be articulated,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Youth Federation launches Eastern Region chapter with 79 youth leaders
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Youth Federation (GYF) has launched its Eastern Regional chapter with 79 youth leaders representing all 33 districts, as the organisation steps up efforts to build a unified platform for youth participation in national development.

The launch, held on Thursday, August 6, 2026, at the Eastern Regional Coordinating Council in Koforidua, also saw the formal outdooring of interim regional executives who will lead the federation’s mobilisation efforts across the region.

The development forms part of GYF’s nationwide rollout of district and regional structures involving youth-led and youth-focused organisations registered with the National Youth Authority (NYA).

Speaking at the ceremony, a representative of the Eastern Regional Minister, Rita Akosua Adjei Awatey, urged young people to work towards a common front to strengthen their influence in engagements with government and political actors.

She said a united youth voice would give young people greater leverage to push for policies and interventions addressing their concerns.

The newly outdoored interim executives also called on participating youth leaders to support the regional mobilisation process, stressing that the responsibility of building the federation could not rest solely with the leadership.

President of the Ghana Youth Federation, Sherif Ghali, described the launch as a significant step towards giving young people a coordinated platform to contribute to national development.

“We have been waiting for a unified voice for a long time — now we have it. Let us unite and contribute to national development. The success of this Federation takes all of us.”

Mr Ghali also outlined the federation’s mandate and national governance structure, explaining the decision to build its regional structures around existing youth-led and youth-focused organisations registered with the NYA.

According to the federation, the approach is intended to strengthen coordination among existing youth groups rather than create parallel structures.

The GYF is established under the National Youth Authority Act, 2016 (Act 939), and operates as a non-profit and non-partisan body representing youth organisations in Ghana.

It works with the National Youth Authority at the district, regional and national levels to advance issues affecting young people.

The participation of 79 youth leaders from all 33 districts was seen by organisers as an indication of interest in a more coordinated approach to youth representation in the Eastern Region.

The next phase will focus on the formation of District Youth Assemblies across the region’s 33 districts.

National Coordinator of the Ghana Youth Federation, Ali Ibraheem, said the district-level structures are expected to pave the way for a Regional Youth Assembly, where substantive regional leadership will be formally constituted and elected.

The Eastern Region launch comes as the GYF continues efforts to strengthen its national institutional presence, including work on its National Strategic Action Plan and representation on youth-related governance structures.

The federation has also been advocating greater youth participation in national processes, including discussions surrounding constitutional reform.

Ghana News.title: Photos: Omane Boamah remembered one year after his death
Ghana News.content:
The late minister's mother (first from left) followed by his widow and three children

The family of the late Defence Minister, Dr Edward Omane Boamah, has marked the first anniversary of his death with a Thanksgiving Service at Christ the King Parish in Accra.

The service brought together government officials, political figures, traditional leaders, colleagues, friends and sympathisers to honour the late minister and reflect on his contribution to Ghana.

Among those present were Deputy Defence Minister Ernest Brogya Genfi, Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu, Lands and Natural Resources Minister Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh and Ghana Cocoa Board CEO Dr Randy Abbey.

Delivering the homily, Rev. Fr Ebenezer Akesseh urged mourners to uphold the values of faith, integrity, selflessness and commitment to the public good, which he said characterised Dr Omane Boamah’s service to the nation.

The family also donated to Christ the King Parish in support of its altar and chaplaincy.

The service ended with prayers for the repose of Dr Omane Boamah’s soul and for strength for his bereaved family and loved ones.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
