World.title: Rare solar eclipse to grace Hungarian skies this week – here is where you can see the most!
World.content:
A rare celestial event is set to light up the skies over Europe next Wednesday, with a solar eclipse visible from Hungary. While a total eclipse will be visible from parts of Spain and Iceland, observers in Hungary will be treated to a spectacular partial eclipse – and those in the western part of the country will have the best view.

Because the eclipse will occur shortly before sunset, location will play a particularly important role in determining how much of the Sun can be seen being covered by the Moon.

Sopron will have the best view

The westernmost parts of Hungary will be in the most favourable position for watching the eclipse. Sopron and its surroundings are expected to offer the best view, with almost 86% of the Sun covered by the Moon before the Sun disappears below the horizon.

The timing of the event means that the further west observers are, the greater the extent of the eclipse they will be able to see.

For comparison, observers in Spain, the Balearic Islands and Iceland will be able to experience a total solar eclipse, while Hungary will remain outside the path of totality. Even so, the partial eclipse promises to be a remarkable sight for anyone interested in astronomy, Időkép writes.

Solar eclipse: Degree of eclipse before sunset. Photo: Időkép

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

How to watch the eclipse safely

Choosing the right location will be essential. Since the Sun will already be very low in the sky, buildings, trees and hills could easily block the view. An open location with a clear, unobstructed western horizon will therefore offer the best chance of seeing the event.

It is also important to protect your eyes.

Never look directly at the Sun without proper certified solar viewing glasses or an appropriate solar filter. The fact that the Sun will be close to setting does not make direct viewing safe.

Clear skies could offer perfect conditions

The weather forecast currently suggests favourable conditions for observing the eclipse, with largely clear and cloudless skies expected across much of Hungary on Wednesday. That could provide excellent viewing conditions for the rare celestial spectacle – even as the country continues to experience hot summer weather.

For those hoping to catch the eclipse, heading to an elevated or otherwise unobstructed location in and around Sopron could offer the most spectacular view Hungary has to offer.

World.title: Sziget 2026: Festival reveals price of budget meals as huge food line-up awaits
World.content:
Sziget Festival is not just about world-famous music acts. This year, the Budapest festival is once again putting a strong emphasis on food, with everything from street food and international favourites to Michelin-starred cuisine on offer. And for festival-goers watching their spending, the popular fixed-price “budget food” option is returning – capped at HUF 3,500 (approx. EUR 10) per meal.

Every year, tens of thousands of people descend on Budapest’s Hajógyári Island for Sziget Festival, with organisers expecting close to 100,000 visitors this year. While the line-up includes major international and Hungarian acts, food has increasingly become an important part of the festival experience.

Budget meals will cost HUF 3,500

Sziget introduced its fixed-price, budget-friendly food initiative a few years ago, giving visitors an affordable alternative to some of the festival’s more expensive dishes.

This year, budget meals will be capped at HUF 3,500, and visitors will be able to buy a one-pot meal for that price, Sziget founder Károly Gerendai told Mindmegette.

The initiative works similarly to fixed-price food options at some of Budapest’s major Christmas markets: participating vendors offer a designated dish at the same maximum price, helping festival-goers keep their food costs under control.

There will be numerous food areas around the festival site, featuring both food trucks and permanent-style food outlets. Visitors can expect classic festival favourites such as hot dogs, burgers and lángos, but also more sophisticated options.

One of the major new additions is Food Paradise, inspired by the concept of Time Out Market. Visitors can eat while DJs provide live entertainment, turning the area into more than just a place to grab a quick bite.

The VIP section will go even further, bringing together some of the best-known names in Budapest’s restaurant scene, including restaurants from the Costes group and 101, as well as dishes associated with venues such as MÁK and Kádár Étkezde.

Photo: Kádár étkezde

Familiar favourites are returning

The 2026 line-up also includes a number of restaurants and food brands that have become familiar faces at festivals and in Budapest’s street-food scene.

Among them is Los Monos, known for its Mexican-inspired food and tacos, while Krumpello will once again demonstrate what can be done with the humble baked potato, serving generously loaded jacket potatoes.

Meraki will bring Greek-inspired dishes and Mediterranean flavours, while Crunchy will cater to fans of crispy, juicy chicken dishes. These are just some of the options available, with the festival promising a broad range of cuisines and styles.

Food Paradise will offer more than a quick festival meal

Food Paradise is expected to be one of the key new food destinations at this year’s Sziget. Rather than simply functioning as a conventional food court, the area is designed as a social and gastronomic hub where visitors can sit down, meet friends and take a proper break between concerts.

The day starts early, too. Between 9 AM and noon, a brunch party will feature breakfast dishes, coffee and DJ sets for early risers. From the afternoon onwards, the focus will shift towards the wider food offering and evening festival atmosphere.

Among the names expected at Food Paradise are 101 Bistro, specialising in modern Asian street food; Tuning Burger; Buja Disznó(k), famous for its schnitzel; Digó, serving Neapolitan-style pizza; Nemo Fish & Chips & Seafood; and á Table, offering pastries and French-inspired dishes.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

Michelin-starred cuisine is also coming to Sziget

One of the festival’s most notable gastronomic additions this year will be found in the VIP area. Costes, one of Hungary’s best-known fine-dining names and associated with Michelin-starred cuisine, will be among the restaurants serving festival-goers.

The VIP food line-up will also include Buja Disznó(k), Digó and 101 Bistro, while TOKIO will bring a more refined take on modern Asian cuisine. It is an unusual combination: one moment you can be watching a major international act, and the next you can be eating food associated with some of Budapest’s leading restaurants.

Sustainability is also on the menu

Sziget is also placing greater emphasis on sustainability across its food operations. The festival will continue its composting programme, which was recognised with an international innovation award in 2019. This year, the system will be extended across all of the festival’s food courts.

Organic waste, as well as the biodegradable plates and cutlery used at the festival, will be collected separately and composted.

The organisers are also requiring participating food vendors to make at least three sustainability commitments. These can include offering vegetarian or vegan main courses, avoiding red meat, using organic ingredients, sourcing products from Hungarian producers or using sustainably sourced palm oil.

A new Green Hospitality Programme will also launch this year, with higher sustainability standards for participating vendors. The first businesses to receive the new certification include Hot by Sophie’s Delight, Vegan Island by Napfényes, Crunchy, Zing Burger & CO, Pasta Vibes and Mambo Pasta Bistro.

A farmers’ market is coming too

For those looking for something fresher after several days of burgers, pizza and lángos, Sziget will also feature its first Farmers’ Market. Local producers will offer fresh vegetables, fruit and other products, giving festival-goers another option beyond traditional festival food.

An Aldi store will also return to the festival, with a full shop built on site. One unusual feature is that visitors will be able to buy fresh meat for grilling and have it prepared for them at the festival. There will also be options for people with dietary restrictions, including gluten-free and/or lactose-free dishes, as well as vegan food.

Sziget food is no longer just about burgers and lángos

Festival food has changed considerably in recent years. What was once largely a choice between a burger, pizza or lángos has evolved into a much broader gastronomic experience.

At Sziget this year, visitors can start the day with brunch and coffee, grab Asian street food in the afternoon, enjoy a Neapolitan pizza before a headline show, or even opt for fine-dining-inspired dishes in the VIP area.

And for those who simply want to eat well without spending a fortune, the HUF 3,500 budget-food option offers a much-needed cheaper alternative. The full list of participating food vendors and further details are available on the official Sziget website.

World.title: Drugging fears emerge after multiple women fall ill during DJ show in Hungary
World.content:
Concerns have emerged over alleged drink spiking at the site of Budapest’s Sziget Festival after several festivalgoers reported that women suddenly became seriously unwell during Hungarian DJ and presenter Balázs Sebestyén’s Saturday night show.

One young man said his sister collapsed and became unresponsive after having a drink at one of the festival’s food and drink outlets. According to reports shared on social media, as many as 18 young women were treated at one medical point with similar symptoms.

The reports have not been independently confirmed as cases of drink spiking, and Hungarian police have reportedly not received an official complaint about such incidents at the festival.

Young woman reportedly collapsed after a drink

Norbert Galambos, who attended the event with his sister and a group of friends, described what happened in a widely shared Facebook post.

According to his account, his sister suddenly collapsed after drinking at a festival bar and stopped responding. When the family sought medical assistance, he said paramedics initially asked how much alcohol she had consumed and whether she had taken drugs.

Galambos stressed that his sister does not use recreational drugs and that she had simply gone to the festival with friends. He also criticised the way he says the pair were treated by medical staff, arguing that his sister was treated as though she had voluntarily taken drugs.

The Hungarian National Ambulance Service shared his post and said it takes the claims seriously and will investigate the circumstances. The service also emphasised that professional medical care should be accompanied by appropriate and empathetic communication with both patients and their concerned relatives.

Reports of more women becoming unwell

According to accounts shared by festivalgoers, the incident may not have been isolated. Witnesses claimed that a number of women experienced similar symptoms and sought medical assistance during the event. One account circulating online claimed that 18 young women were treated at a single medical point.

However, this figure has not been independently verified, and it remains unclear how many people may actually have been affected or what caused their symptoms. Another festivalgoer, a 39-year-old woman named Enikő, also described becoming suddenly ill during the DJ show.

She said she had asked someone to bring drinks from a VIP area because of the long queues at the festival bars. She claimed that shortly afterwards she became severely unwell and lost control of her movements. According to her account, her husband and another couple who happened to be nearby helped her until medical assistance arrived. She later said she was convinced that her symptoms were not simply the result of drinking alcohol.

What is GHB?

Some of the social media reports have suggested that GHB, sometimes known as “Gina”, may have been involved. However, there is currently no confirmed evidence establishing that GHB was responsible for the reported incidents.

GHB is a synthetic psychoactive substance that is colourless and odourless in liquid form. It can cause drowsiness, confusion and impaired consciousness, while larger amounts can result in unconsciousness and potentially life-threatening breathing problems.

Combining GHB with alcohol can be particularly dangerous because both substances can depress the central nervous system. The drug has also been associated with sexual assaults and robberies because a person under its influence may become extremely vulnerable and unable to protect themselves.

Importantly, the symptoms described by festivalgoers alone cannot establish what substance, if any, was involved. Medical assessment and toxicological testing would be needed to determine the cause.

GHB can disappear from the body quickly

According to Blikk, one difficulty in investigating suspected GHB exposure is the substance’s relatively short detection window.

GHB can generally only be detected in blood for a few hours after consumption and in urine for several more hours. This means that if someone suspects they have been drugged, seeking medical attention as soon as possible can be important. A hair test may potentially detect GHB exposure much later, but such testing is more specialised and costly.

No official police complaint reported so far

Despite the growing number of social media posts, there has so far been no confirmed report of an official police complaint concerning drink spiking at Sziget, according to the reports available. The claims therefore remain allegations at this stage.

The Hungarian National Ambulance Service is investigating the circumstances surrounding the treatment of the reported patients, while the exact number of people affected and the cause of their symptoms remain unclear.

Festivalgoers are nevertheless being urged to take sensible precautions, including keeping an eye on their drinks, staying with friends and seeking medical help immediately if they or someone in their group suddenly becomes confused, severely drowsy, unconscious or otherwise seriously unwell.

If you missed it: Transylvanian villagers attack ambulance after seeing TikTok rumours about kidnapping children

Sziget not aware of drugging incidents

Sziget also responded to the above reports. In their response to Daily News Hungary, they stated that medical services were provided during the event in cooperation with the National Ambulance Service. Of the more than 60,000 visitors, fewer than 100 required medical attention; of these, 20 cases were alcohol-related, and there were no drug-related incidents.

“We, too, were deeply outraged by the reports that appeared on social media, and we encourage anyone affected by such an incident to contact the police. For our part, we will do everything we can to assist the investigative authorities in their work,” they wrote.

They also noted that their catering units have been working with the same tried-and-true, reliable subcontractors for years, who serve the public safely and to a high standard.

World.title: Ferencváros narrowly beaten by Real Madrid at packed Groupama Arena
World.content:
Ferencváros suffered a narrow 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid in a high-profile friendly at Budapest’s Groupama Arena on Saturday, but the Hungarian champions gave their illustrious opponents plenty to think about and found the net through Kenan Kodro.

Fradi impress against European giants

Real Madrid took control late in the first half when Mario Rivas headed the visitors in front, before Carlos Espí doubled their advantage shortly after the interval. Ferencváros responded through Kodro in the 57th minute and grew into the game, but could not find the equaliser.

The result nevertheless represented a memorable occasion for Ferencváros, who welcomed one of football’s most decorated clubs to their home ground.

Groupama Arena turns white and green

The match attracted an unusually large number of Real Madrid supporters, with fans wearing shirts bearing the names of stars such as Federico Valverde, Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Rodrygo.

Inside the stadium, Real Madrid shirts were considerably more prominent than usual alongside Ferencváros’ traditional green-and-white colours.

On the pitch, however, the colours were reversed. Ferencváros wore a new pale-gold and off-white kit, while Real Madrid appeared in green. The atmosphere was lively from the start, with the stadium filling rapidly before kick-off.

Real Madrid dominate but Fradi stand firm

Ferencváros did not appear intimidated by their illustrious opponents and created several promising attacks in the opening stages, although their efforts failed to seriously trouble the Madrid goal.

As the first half progressed, Real increasingly controlled possession. Their quick passing and explosive movement forced Ferencváros deeper, with the visitors repeatedly attempting shots from distance.

The hosts’ first major defensive test came in the 36th minute, when Endrick found space in the area, only for goalkeeper Dénes Dibusz to keep out his close-range effort.

Real’s pressure finally produced a goal in the 41st minute. Arda Güler’s corner reached Alexis Ciria, who returned the ball into the danger area, allowing Mario Rivas to head Madrid into the lead.

Madrid’s stars make their mark

The second half brought a major change in personnel for the Spanish giants, with Vinícius Júnior, Dean Huijsen, Antonio Rüdiger, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Carlos Espí and Bernardo Silva among those introduced.

The arrival of several established stars immediately increased Madrid’s attacking threat. After an impressive passing move, Federico Valverde provided the final pass for Carlos Espí, who finished calmly to make it 2-0.

Ferencváros responded quickly. In the 57th minute, Kristoffer Zachariassen delivered an excellent cross from the right, and Kenan Kodro met it at the near post to fire the ball into the bottom-left corner. The Groupama Arena erupted, with even some Real Madrid supporters applauding the home side’s goal.

Fradi push for an equaliser

The goal changed the complexion of the match. Ferencváros began escaping the pressure that had characterised much of the first half and regularly worked their way towards Madrid’s penalty area.

Zachariassen came close again with a header, but his effort went straight into the hands of goalkeeper Andriy Lunin.

Real continued to threaten from set pieces, with Trent Alexander-Arnold, Federico Valverde and Güler among those around a late free-kick. Güler ultimately sent his effort over the crossbar.

As the final whistle approached, Ferencváros looked capable of finding an equaliser, with the flow of the game suggesting they were closer to making it 2-2 than Real were to extending their lead. The second goal ultimately failed to arrive.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

Encouraging test ahead of European football

Real Madrid therefore left Budapest with a 2-1 victory, but Ferencváros can take considerable encouragement from their performance.

The Hungarian side competed well against one of the world’s biggest clubs, absorbed sustained pressure, scored against Madrid after the interval and created chances to level the match.

The friendly was nevertheless only part of a busy summer schedule. Ferencváros’ attention now turns to the return leg against Górnik Zabrze in Europa League qualifying.

That fixture will carry far greater competitive importance, but after their performance against Real Madrid, Fradi can approach it with plenty of confidence.

World.title: ‘We were told what was good for us’: Hungarian minister vows to change attitudes towards disabled people
World.content:
Ensuring physical and digital accessibility “is my pet project”, the minister of social and family affairs said on Facebook on Sunday, after receiving visually impaired guests from south-eastern Hungary’s Békés county at his ministry.

In his post, the minister slammed the previous government by saying that people living with a handicap “were not in the focus” in the past 16 years.

“Accessibility and equal opportunities were strongly suppressed; we were paternalised and told what was good for us,” the minister, who is visually impaired himself, said. He added he would work to change those attitudes and asked civil organisations to signal problems.

Meanwhile, Kátai-Németh said it was crucial to provide jobs for the handicapped.

World.title: Transylvanian villagers attack ambulance after seeing TikTok rumours about kidnapping children
World.content:
An ambulance crew was attacked with stones, sticks and axes in a Transylvanian village after residents reportedly mistook the emergency vehicle for one allegedly linked to an online kidnapping rumour.

Angry Transylvanian villagers attack emergency vehicle with stones, sticks and axes

The incident took place on Saturday evening in Recea-Cristur, a village in Transylvania region’s Cluj County around 40 kilometres from the city of Dej.

Romania’s Health Ministry said on Sunday that the ambulance was attacked amid unfounded rumours circulating on TikTok about so-called “black ambulances” allegedly being used by organ traffickers to abduct children. The ambulance driver suffered a serious eye injury during the attack.

Ambulance blocked by two cars

The Cluj County Ambulance Service vehicle had travelled to Recea-Cristur to collect a patient. According to the accounts cited by Romanian authorities, the crew encountered hostility as soon as they arrived in the village. Residents reportedly filmed the ambulance on their mobile phones while the crew was trying to find the patient’s address.

The situation escalated when two cars were allegedly used to block the ambulance in the centre of the Transylvanian village, forcing the vehicle to stop. Several people then reportedly attacked the ambulance using stones, sticks and axes.

The emergency crew’s doctor said they may have faced an even more serious situation had the driver not managed to turn the ambulance around and escape in the opposite direction.

Romanian ambulance vehicle. Illustration. Featured image: depositphotos.com

Driver taken to operating theatre

After the crew reached hospital in Dej, the ambulance driver also required medical treatment. A fragment of the vehicle’s shattered windscreen reportedly struck the driver’s eye and injured the cornea. The driver subsequently underwent surgery.

The incident has highlighted the potentially serious consequences of rumours targeting emergency services, particularly when false claims spread rapidly through social-media platforms.

Authorities link attack to TikTok rumours

Police said the attack in Transylvania was connected to unfounded rumours circulating on TikTok claiming that organ traffickers were travelling around Romanian communities in ambulances in order to abduct children.

Romanian authorities have repeatedly rejected the claims and urged the public to rely on verified information from official sources rather than unconfirmed social-media posts.

The Romanian Interior Ministry issued another warning on Sunday, publishing screenshots of three TikTok posts promoting claims about the so-called “black ambulance”.

According to the ministry, photographs used in the posts as supposed “warnings” had been manipulated or generated using artificial intelligence.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

Authorities: no recorded case of an ambulance being used for kidnapping

In its warning, Romania’s Interior Ministry said that the country had never recorded a case in which an ambulance was used to abduct people.

The ministry stressed that ambulances are operated by medical professionals whose role is to save lives, and warned that misinformation can have consequences beyond simply causing public anxiety.

False rumours, it said, can place emergency workers in danger when they are responding to calls for help. The authorities therefore urged members of the public not to share alarming claims without checking their authenticity.

More on the region: Hungarian journalist attacked by bear near Fidesz’s annual Transylvanian festival

Misinformation puts emergency workers at risk

For ambulance crews, reaching a patient quickly can be a matter of life and death. Any attempt to block an emergency vehicle, intimidate its crew or prevent it from leaving an area can potentially delay medical assistance.

In this case, according to the authorities and the medical workers’ account, the ambulance crew was able to escape and reach the hospital, but the driver sustained a serious injury in the process.

Romanian officials have once again called on the public to verify information before sharing it online, warning that manipulated images and AI-generated content can make false stories appear credible.

World.title: Seven Romanians placed in detention after attacking an ambulance in Cluj County
World.content:
Six men and one woman were placed in pre-trial detention after attacking an ambulance in Cluj County, central Romania, amid a backdrop of disinformation on TikTok regarding black ambulances that allegedly steal children.

The attack occurred in the village of Recea-Cristur, Cluj County, on Saturday, August 8. The incident began when the medical crew stopped after entering the locality to ask residents for directions to a patient's address.

Soon after, according to the Department for Emergency Situations, the ambulance that was transporting a patient to hospital was intentionally blocked by two cars. Several people reportedly got out carrying clubs and axes and began attacking the ambulance, accusing the crew of operating the alleged "black ambulance that steals children."

The police were called, and the ambulance crew managed to continue its mission and transport the patient safely to the Emergency Unit.

As a result of the assault, the driver of the ambulance suffered ocular trauma, which required specialist medical evaluation and a surgical intervention during the night

A day later, the Dej Court decided to place six men and one woman in pre-trial detention. The woman is being investigated for disturbing public order and peace and for assault or other acts of violence, while the men are being investigated for disturbing public order and peace.

In response to the attack, DSU drew attention to the danger posed by false information regarding the activity of ambulances and emergency services on social media. “Such claims are false and deeply dangerous,” the service said in the press release.

Also on Sunday, deputy prime minister Oana Gheorghiu said that Romania needs a strong law against online disinformation and manipulation. “Ambulances do not steal children, but TikTok steals brains,” she also wrote on Facebook.

Similarly, Romania’s Ministry of Interior noted that no cases have been recorded in Romania in which ambulances were involved in the kidnapping of persons. MAI warned that the videos and images on social media are modified or entirely created using artificial intelligence.

Last month, Romanian president Nicusor Dan argued that Romanian legislation should be adapted to resist the spread of false information.

World.title: Constanţa County Council advances with project of EUR 23 mln Aquarium
World.content:
The Constanţa County Council has entered the implementation stage of one of the most important investment projects in the field of tourism and education in the region, after signing the financing contract for the new Aquarium of the Constanţa Natural Sciences Museum Complex, according to Ziarul Financiar.

The project has a total value of RON 115.02 million (approximately EUR 23 million, including VAT) and benefits from financing through the South-East Regional Program 2021–2027. The works will have an estimated duration of 24 months, and the implementation deadline is set for December 2029.

The project includes the development of pools dedicated to the Planetary Ocean and the Black Sea, underwater viewing tunnels, a penguin habitat, thematic exhibitions, a conference room, a library, a café, and modern spaces for educational and scientific activities.

World.title: Ambulance attacked in Romania amid viral TikTok child-stealing hoax
World.content:
An ambulance crew was attacked with sticks, axes and stones in Recea Cristur, Cluj County, after false claims circulated on TikTok that an ambulance was being used to steal children, according to Romanian authorities and Curs de Guvernare.

The ambulance driver was injured in the eye by shards of broken glass after the vehicle was attacked and required emergency surgery in Cluj-Napoca. The doctors said he suffered corneal damage and would need at least three months to recover.

The incident began when the medical crew stopped after entering the locality to ask residents for directions to a patient's address. Police said the ambulance appeared similar to vehicles shown in TikTok videos spreading false claims that children were being abducted for organ harvesting and medical experiments.

After the medical team collected the patient and began travelling towards Dej Hospital, where the patient was due to be transported, their route was blocked by a car. Several people reportedly got out carrying clubs and axes and began attacking the ambulance, accusing the crew of operating the alleged "black ambulance that steals children".

The attack has prompted renewed calls from the government for legislation addressing disinformation and harmful content on social media.

Acting Defence Minister Radu Miruță urged Chamber of Deputies President Sorin Grindeanu to put forward for debate and rapid adoption a bill he submitted in March 2025 aimed at limiting the spread of manipulative and illegal content on social networks, according to Euronews.

"The law against disinformation must be adopted! I submitted it to Parliament in 2025. It passed tacitly in the Senate and is blocked in the Chamber of Deputies," Miruță said.

World.title: Romania’s Liberal Party ready to back government of technocrats with transparent majority
World.content:
Romania’s Liberal Party (PNL) would support a possible technocratic government, the party's president and acting PM Ilie Bolojan told RFI.

The interim prime minister, however, sets some conditions: the incoming government should have transparent majority parliamentary support, at least for a defined period of time, and it should come with a ruling agenda that maintains the strategy of controlling state spending and reducing deficits.

“The sooner we have a government, the better for this country, and each of us has a responsibility to seek solutions for this," PM Bolojan said.

The statement came after Social Democrat leader Ilie Grineanu announced an imminent ruling majority that his party will make public after August 15.

Ilie Bolojan has repeatedly stressed that it is the Social Democrats’ responsibility to come up with a new government, after it joined the Alliance for Unity of Romanians (AUR) in the no-confidence motion against the government.

Nearly 90 days after the dismissal of the government on May 5 and two unsuccessful appointments made by president Nicusor Dan, there is no consensus for the future government team.

PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu will have more discussions with the President by the end of the week, according to sources in the party leadership consulted by HotNews. Sources expect a prime minister appointment to be made next month at the latest. The Social Democrats are working on forming a majority to support a possible single-party PSD government.

World.title: Romania’s slot-machine sector shrinks sharply after new local rules
World.content:
Romania’s authorised slot-machine sector has contracted sharply following new regulations that transferred greater powers over gambling authorisation to local authorities, with only 2,337 slot-machine stations authorised between February and May 2026, compared with 18,981 in the same period of 2025, according to data cited by Profit.ro.

This seems, however, to be the indirect effect of the public debate rather than direct constraints of city halls that gained greater power: only a few of them have imposed restrictions so far.

The decline follows the entry into force of Emergency Ordinance 7/2026, which gives city halls greater authority to allow or prohibit gambling activities in their jurisdictions. The changes have also reduced the number of gaming devices currently operating and the associated tax revenues.

Of 45,659 gaming devices authorised across Romania in 2025, 29,014 remain in operation, according to the data. This represents around 64% of last year's authorised stock.

The reduction has occurred despite limited implementation of the new local rules. Only 90 of roughly 3,100 administrative-territorial units have so far adopted local council decisions on gambling, even though the 60-day deadline for issuing such decisions expired more than two months ago.

Of those 90 decisions, 35 prohibit gambling activities, while 55 allow them to continue, according to the data cited by Profit.ro.

The contraction has also affected public revenues from gambling authorisation fees. Operators paid RON 485 million in such fees between February and May 2025, compared with RON 300 million during the corresponding period of 2026.

The new rules have therefore reduced the number of authorised machines before most local authorities have formally decided whether gambling activities should be permitted in their jurisdictions.

The government introduced the changes as part of wider efforts to regulate the gambling sector and give local authorities greater control over where gambling businesses can operate.

World.title: Romania says voluntary power savings cut evening demand by up to 300 MW
World.content:
Romania reduced electricity consumption by around 200-300 MW during evening peak hours this week as households, companies and public institutions responded to government calls to conserve energy, prime minister and acting Energy Minister Ilie Bolojan said, cited by B1TV.

Bolojan said evening consumption, which in previous years typically reached around 7,700-8,000 MW, was recorded at between 7,300 MW and 7,700 MW on most days this week. He said the reduction was significant as domestic electricity production does not always cover peak demand.

The reduction was recorded on almost every day except one when high temperatures drove increased use of air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment in shops and warehouses, Bolojan said.

The government has appealed to large industrial consumers to voluntarily reduce electricity use between 19:00 and 23:00 as Romania faces pressure on its power system amid low Danube flows and reduced availability from its Cernavoda nuclear plant.

Municipalities and companies in Romania responded to the government's call for reducing electricity consumption.

Donalam, part of the AFV Beltrame Group, said it had adjusted the operating schedules of its units in Călăraşi and Târgovişte in response to the government's request. The steel producer will reduce electricity consumption during the evening peak period, according to a company statement.

Automobile manufacturers Dacia and Ford have also helped ease demand after bringing forward their annual August maintenance shutdowns. The temporary production stoppages at their plants in Mioveni and Craiova reduce electricity consumption during a period of heightened pressure on the national system.

The government has also prepared a mechanism allowing certain large industrial consumers to be disconnected from the grid with 24 hours' notice if available generation is insufficient to cover projected demand. Household consumers and facilities whose operations cannot be interrupted, including hospitals and certain energy infrastructure, are excluded.

Bolojan thanked consumers, companies and public institutions that had responded to the conservation measures as the authorities continue to monitor electricity supply and demand.

World.title: Romania’s works on Danube ease risks of future shutdown of Cernavodă nuclear plant
World.content:
The Danube level close to Romania’s Cernavodă nuclear plant increased by some 8 cm compared to the projected level after two barges were sunk to change the water flow, the manager of the nuclear plant, Romeo Urjan, announced, cited by Digi24 on Sunday, August 9.

The updated forecast indicated at that moment that the plant could keep functioning for another nine days before full shutdown under the conditions of low Danube flow rates – compared to four to five days estimated previously.

The effects of the latter two of the total of four barges sunk in a complex operation aimed at diverting more water to the Danube arm supplying water to Cernavodă could be visible on Monday, August 10, according to the Romanian Waters National Administration Company, which participated in the operations.

Under the current record low levels of Danube affecting more nuclear plants in the region that use the river’s water for cooling, Cernavodă NPP keeps in operation only one of its two reactors with a net output of 680 MW, roughly one tenth of the peak national consumption.

The second unit’s shutdown could force Transelectrica to gradually disconnect industrial users under a mechanism legislated by the Government last week.

"The danger has not passed; the Danube currents are strong and can be very unpredictable. At any moment, the barges can be displaced from their current position, and the redirection of the additional flow to Cernavodă can be reduced (or even cancelled)," warned in a Facebook post Ionel Scrioşteanu, who coordinated the action on the Danube.

In related news, Transelectrica announced that Romania managed to cover its peak consumption and even export energy during strong output contributed by the wind farms on the evening of August 8, and the favourable situation continued on the morning of Sunday, August 9. The wind farms were generating above 2 GW at that time, while their output fell again under 600 MW on the morning of August 10.

World.title: Moody’s affirms Romania’s sovereign rating, sees risks of slower fiscal consolidation
World.content:
International rating agency Moody’s on August 7 affirmed Romania’s fragile Baa3 sovereign rating, along with its negative outlook, linked to high implementation risks related to the country’s ambitious multi-year fiscal consolidation programme. Compared to a year ago, the fiscal deficit narrowed faster than expected, but there is less clarity on further steps towards a sustainable deficit, the rating agency concluded.

Just like Fitch a week before, Moody’s signalled that the political consensus on fiscal consolidation beyond 2026 emerged as the key driver for further rating actions, despite the fiscal consolidation having outperformed expectations so far.

While Romania managed to reduce the deficit somewhat more quickly than Moody’s expected in its September 2025 country update, the rating agency assesses political conditions as more challenging following the passage of the no-confidence vote against the government in May.

The rating agency remarks that political fragmentation has delayed the formation of a new government, but expressed expectations that a new administration will take office after the summer break.

Moody’s says that passage of a deficit-reducing 2027 budget before the end of 2026 and of an adequate public wage law would signal political consensus in favour of implementing and maintaining a large fiscal effort beyond 2026. The outlook could return to stable if it is clear that such a political consensus still exists in favour of implementing and maintaining a large fiscal effort beyond 2026.

Conversely, “a political and policymaking environment that is unlikely to be conducive to sustaining a large fiscal effort over a number of years” would exert negative pressure (prompting a downgrade to non-investment region).

Separately, the rating agency notes risks stemming from geopolitical risk emanating from the war in Ukraine or any other developments that could jeopardise the funding of the country’s wide current account deficit, with a negative impact on its rating.

Technically, Moody’s expects Romania's 2026 headline deficit to decline significantly to 5.8% of GDP this year, down over two percentage points in one year, thanks to expenditure restraint and revenues holding up in spite of challenging macroeconomic conditions.

Despite the slightly faster-than-expected deficit reduction, the rating agency expects Romania's interest burden will still increase in the coming years given high financing needs and the prevalence of market-based funding. Interest costs will increase to 3.3% of GDP in 2028 from 2.8% of GDP in 2025, up from 2.0% of GDP in 2023.

As a result of still elevated primary deficits and rising interest costs, Moody’s expects the debt burden to continue to increase, albeit at a slower pace than it anticipated at the time of its last rating committee in September 2025. Just like Fitch, Moody’s projects debt will increase to 64.5% of GDP in 2028 (above the projected peer median of 57.9%) from 59.3% in 2025. The rating agency’s current baseline assumes a gradual further reduction in deficits that stabilises the debt burden at around 66% of GDP by the end of this decade.

World.title: In Solving World War II ‘Puzzle’, Young Greeks Help ‘Heal a Wound’
World.content:
After wading through the archives at Arolsen, municipal registers, the Internet and other documents, the tram was able to return a wristwatch to the family of Vangelis Kerasiotis, who spent time in a forced labour camp in Germany in 1944, aged 19.

Having worked at the camp as an interpreter, Kerasiotis returned to Greece in 1945, where he moved in with a Jewish woman and joined the police. He died at the age of 25.

“The objects are of zero value in terms of their literal value, but they are of enormous value in terms of mental upliftment,” said his niece, Chrysanthi Kerasotou, who received the watch with her sister and mother during an event organised by the Greek government in late June.

Hotzidis, a historian, said that between 50,000 and 60,000 Greek Jews perished in the Nazi camps and at least 10,000 other Greeks were sent to labour camps, including leftists involved in the resistance against the Nazi occupation of Greece.

“We do not know if Kerasiotis was engaged in any political activity,” Hotzidis said. “The relatives did not mention anything, but even if wasn’t, his name was certainly heard somewhere by Greek collaborators of the German battalion security forces and some gendarmes who collaborated with the Germans.”

“It is important to remember, because this way we know not only our recent history, but we can think that it is good that all these events do not happen again,” he said. “So, first we must know them and secondly remember them, ensuring they are never forgotten.”

In Arolsen, Meiwes said that some 2,000 envelopes remain. For some, they known neither the nationality nor the identity of the person whose belonging are inside.

“It is possible that some of these still belong to Greek nationals,” she told BIRN.

The Nazis turned people into numbers, Meiwes said, so it is important “to give them back their names and to tell their stories”.

World.title: A Decade After North Macedonia’s Deadliest Floods, Dangers Remain
World.content:
On August 6, 2016 torrential rain triggered a devastating flash flood in the north-east outskirts of Skopje, killing 22 people and causing more than 30 million euros in damage.

Suburbs of the capital like Singelic and Cento, villages like Stajkovci and Aracinovo, and surrounding areas were among the worst hit, as torrents of water and mud swept through streets and homes within minutes.

“We narrowly escaped death. The water was almost two metres deep. I have never seen this kind of weather,” one Stajkovci resident said at the time. “It was terrible. We had only half a minute to get outside [the house] and save ourselves when the water surged,” said another.

In the aftermath, experts pointed to several factors that had turned an extreme weather event into a disaster. Around 93 litres of rain per square metre fell on the heavily deforested southern slopes of Skopska Crna Gora Mountain in just four hours, allowing water and mud to rush towards the settlements below.

World.title: Albania Could Face Costly Arbitration Battle After Scrapping Vlora Airport Plans
World.content:
An international arbitration dispute is looming after Albania’s Ministry of Infrastructure and Energy announced last week that it has officially started the procedure to terminate the concession contract for Vlora International Airport.

The decision follows a bitter legal tussle between the two consortium partners, Mabco Construction and 2A Group, which began in the autumn of 2025 over a dispute concerning the division of shares between them.

There have also been large confrontations between workers from the two companies over access to the site, and a series of court rulings. The deadlock persisted even after the Supreme Court in May rejected 2A Group's requests for interim measures to secure its lawsuit. That decision was later followed by additional blocking rulings issued by the Court of First Instance Tirana.

World.title: Albanian Court Puts Turkish Activist in Custody After Extradition Demand
World.content:
Protesters rally with pictures of victims of the 2013 Gezi Park protests in Istanbul, April 2022. Photo: EPA-EFE/SEDAT SUNA.

The Tirana Court on Friday ordered a custody remand for Julide Yazici, who is wanted for extradition by Turkey to serve a prison sentence for aiding a terrorist organisation – charges that she claims are motivated by her political activism.

Yazici was arrested on August 4 at Tirana Airport while travelling from France to Albania after it was discovered that she was wanted for extradition to Turkey.

The judge granted the prosecution’s custody request despite Yazici’s lawyer’s arguments that his client “holds political asylum status in France and poses no danger”, and could be placed under house arrest instead.

The lawyer, Artan Shllaku, said that the decision will be appealed.

Shllaku added that Yazici, who teaches at an elementary school in France, had visited Albania a year earlier to see relatives and had encountered no issues.

Yazici is wanted by Turkish authorities to serve the remainder of a four-year prison sentence – three years, five months and 22 days – for providing logistical support to and participating in a terrorist organisation.

According to a decision by the French National Court of Asylum dated November 2020, a document obtained by BIRN, Yazici was involved in political activism in Turkey and participated in the Gezi Park mass protests in 2013 against the administration led by Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

She actively supported the former People’s Democratic Party, HDP, a left-wing political group that supported Turkey’s Kurdish minority, and which later became the DEM Party.

The French court decision granting asylum to Yazici stated that she was arrested in January 2016 “for having allowed a young woman she did not know, who had been introduced to her by a friend, to stay in her student room”.

The French court decision in the document that Yazici had “a well-founded fear … of being persecuted if she returns to her country due to her political activism”.

Yazici is not the first Turkish national to be arrested in Albania for extradition in controversial circumstances in recent years. Teachers and others linked to the movement previously led by the now-deceased cleric Fethullah Gulen, which is classified as a terrorist organisation by the authorities under Erdogan, have also been detained and then deported in line with Ankara’s demands.

World.title: Secrecy Surrounds Croatia’s Arrest of Alleged Serbian State-Linked Hacker
World.content:
Photo illustration: EPA/SASCHA STEINBACH.

The Croatian and Serbian authorities are remaining tight-lipped over the arrest last week of a Serbian businessman named as Georgije V., 33, on suspicion of hacking into the computer systems of various Croatian state institutions and public agencies.

The Serbian man is reportedly suspected of hacking into the Croatian Interior Ministry, the Central Register of Pension-Insured Persons, the Croatian Health Insurance Fund, the Croatian Regulatory Agency for Network Activities, the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute, the Croatian Tax Administration and the Croatian Automobile Club.

Tomo Medved, the Minister of Croatian Veterans, was asked about the case on Friday but declined to provide details.

“I would like to commend the entire security and intelligence system for its responsible and vigilant monitoring and protection of the interests of the Republic of Croatia. Given the ongoing proceedings, I cannot comment further than that,” Medved told journalists.

Croatian daily Jutarnji list has reported that the arrest took place on July 28, when Georgije V. was on holiday in Croatia. He had arrived with his wife, two children and mother at a tourist resort on the Adriatic coast a few days earlier.

Following his arrest, police searched his electronic devices, vehicle and accommodation under court orders. They seized items and digital data allegedly linking him to criminal acts, including two mobile phones and a laptop containing a large amount of data.

The court ordered one month of pre-trial detention, despite the man offering 20,000 euros in bail money and his family home in Novi Sad as collateral.

Croatia’s Chief State Attorney, Ivan Turudic, initially sparked public interest on Monday when he made a comment about a case related to national security. It was then reported by Jutarnji list that Turudic was referring to the arrest of an alleged hacker linked to Serbia’s Security Intelligence Agency, BIA.

It is not known whether the suspect’s alleged access to the computer systems of various institutions and agencies endangered Croatia’s national security in any way, or what he did with any data he may have obtained.

Nera Gajdarov Beg, the suspect’s lawyer, told Jutarnji list that the court’s custody order is being contested.

“An appeal has been filed against the decision to order pretrial detention because we believe that not all legal requirements for such a decision have been met. At this point, I cannot provide details of the defence because the proceedings are in the investigation phase, which is secret,” Gajdarov Beg said.

The Serbian authorities have not commented on the arrest so far. However, Serbian media have reported that Georgije V. is the owner of an active Novi Sad-based company specialising in computer programming and cybersecurity.

World.title: Croatian Serb Leader Deplores Hate Speech at Operation Storm Commemoration
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

Milorad Pupovac, president of the Independent Democratic Serb Party, SDSS, and MP, on Friday said that slogans and chants heard on the streets of Knin on August 5, the day marking the 31st anniversary of Operation Storm, represented a “serious attack on constitutional values and democracy”.

Pupovac, leader of the main party representing Serbs in Croatia, argued that “hatred and incitement to crime are incompatible with true patriotism”.

At a press conference, he showed a compilation of recordings from Knin, the town that was the headquarters of a rebel Serbian statelet crushed by the Croatian Army’s Operation Storm in 1995.

They included sports fans and army veterans singing songs glorifying the Ustasha – the army of the Independent State of Croatia, NDH, a World War II fascist puppet state operating under the patronage of Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy.

The recordings also showed people chanting: “We Croats do not drink wine, only the blood of Chetniks [Serbian nationalists] from Knin”; “The battle is fought, it is fought, the Ustasha flag is flying”, as well as insults directed at St Sava, the patron saint of the Serbian Orthodox Church.

“Those who have been trying to pass this off as an act of patriotism for years are actually seriously violating the true values of patriotism. In peacetime, the greatest patriotic virtue is constitutional patriotism,” Pupovac said.

He added that such behaviour was a “vicious attack on democracy”.

The SNV cited articles of the Croatian Constitution that it believes were violated by the shouting of the Ustasha salute “For the Homeland, Ready” and other glorifications of the NDH. The violations came after, not during, the official anniversary celebrations, it said.

Every year, Knin hosts a commemoration of Operation Storm, which liberated about 18 per cent of Croatia’s territory from rebel Serb forces and was followed by the flight of around 200,000 Serbs from Croatia. Some of them later returned.

SDSS leader Pupovac also criticised the Croatian judicial authorities, questioning why the State Attorney’s Office often does not react to hate speech and incitement to violence, appealing for an end to what he called a policy of appeasement.

He warned that failure to condemn such phenomena represents a direct threat to the Serb community in Croatia, and to all citizens who advocate for a state governed by the rule of law.

World.title: Week in Review: The Electoral Merry-Go-Round
World.content:
Last week, a no-confidence motion in the Serbian government was held in the country’s parliament. A boisterous discussion ensued between ruling and opposition MPs, but the motion failed – as expected.

Its real significance was not so much the outcome as the fact that the holding the vote, tabled at the beginning of the year, cleared an important obstacle to calling early parliamentary elections.

President Aleksandar Vucic has fuelled speculation that polls are imminent. Our analysis takes a look a look at what will determine when they happen – and whether they will happen at all.

World.title: Isamaa, EKRE and Center agree on new Pärnu coalition
World.content:
Isamaa, EKRE and the Center Party have reached an agreement to form a new governing coalition in Pärnu, Pärnu City Council Chair Andrei Korobeinik said.

The coalition agreement between the three parties will be signed at Villa Ammende at noon on Tuesday, when the coalition's main agreements and Pärnu's new city leaders will also be presented.

During nearly two weeks of negotiations, the three parties have agreed on the principles of the new coalition, the division of responsibilities and its key objectives. The final round of negotiations will take place Tuesday morning.

At a public press conference beginning at noon, representatives of Isamaa, EKRE and the Center Party will sign the coalition agreement and present its key provisions. The composition of the new city government and the allocation of political areas of responsibility will also be announced.

The new coalition will hold a total of 22 seats on the 39-member Pärnu City Council.

An extraordinary meeting of the Pärnu City Council to replace the city's leadership is scheduled for Monday, August 17.

In late July, Center's Andrei Korobeinik accused Mayor Kristel Voltenberg of cutting short discussions on the functioning of the coalition and violating agreements. Last week, EKRE, the Center Party and Isamaa submitted a motion of no confidence in Voltenberg.

Kristel Voltenberg. Source: Haide Rannakivi/Pärnu City Government

Prior to this shift, Pärnu was governed by a broad, fragile 5-partner coalition formed following the 2025 local elections. It included EKRE, Center and Parempoolsed, as well as the local elections alliances Pärnu with Heart, of Mayor Kristel Voltenberg, and Pärnu Unites. The 5-member administration was plagued by internal friction and ideological divides across its broad spectrum of members.

World.title: Arnold Rutto: A memory operation, Caucasus‑style
World.content:
The pipes of Tbilisi's Rike Park, whose demolition began in Georgia this August, were controversial, expensive, unfinished, politically charged — but they were symbolic, writes Arnold Rutto.

Anyone who has ever visited Tbilisi could not pass by the futuristic pipes of Rike Park without noticing them. Those two giant metal tunnels, designed by Italian architects Massimiliano and Doriana Fuksas, stood right next to the Bridge of Peace as the boldest and most distinctive symbol of contemporary architecture in Tbilisi.

The building, which was once supposed to become a concert hall and exhibition space, was left unfinished due to political changes and stood closed for years. Now, in August, demolition has begun, with completion planned for December 2026.

This act erases from Tbilisi's cityscape a trace of a specific era — President Mikheil Saakashvili's modernization period, when Georgia moved clearly and confidently toward a European direction.

Although that innovative period did not pass without painful setbacks — including the 2008 war, the loss of the Kodori Gorge to Abkhazia, and the loss of control over other disputed territories — it was still a time when the country sought to define itself as part of the European cultural sphere.

The Rike Park music and exhibition center was built as part of Saakashvili's modernization program. During construction, the project was estimated to cost around 40 million euros, and the Georgian state spent about 75 million lari of public money on it, which corresponds to roughly 25 million euros at today's exchange rate. The building was never opened and remained empty after the 2012 change of government.

"Something is being removed from the cityscape that reminds people of a time when Georgia chose a European path."

The Fuksas architecture was neither accidental nor neutral. Massimiliano and Doriana Fuksas's work is visible in many European cities and beyond — for example, the Lyon Confluence residential complex in France, New Rome /EUR convention centre and hotel the Cloud in Italy, Vienna's Twin Tower, modern shopping centers in Turin, and the Shenzhen Bao'an Airport terminal 3 built through international cooperation.

All these buildings carry the same idea: openness, forward‑looking boldness, the aesthetics of European modernism. The Rike Park pipes fit into this logic. They were Tbilisi's attempt to step into the same architectural class as Europe's major cities. That is precisely why their demolition is a memory‑political decision.

After the change of government, the building was essentially frozen. Georgia's current political course differs significantly from Saakashvili's Euro‑Atlantic vision, and critics argue that the country has moved away from its earlier clearly pro‑European direction. Against this backdrop, the demolition of the Rike Park pipes becomes a symbolic act: something is being removed from the cityscape that reminds people of a time when Georgia chose a European path.

With this demolition, what Saakashvili's government built is being taken down and removed from the city's visual memory. It erases a stage of the city's history and architecture — and is simultaneously an attempt to erase an entire era from spatial memory.

History offers a painful parallel. During Soviet rule, numerous churches, monasteries, and other historical sites in Georgia were destroyed or altered because they were considered ideologically unsuitable. Religious and national symbols did not fit the worldview of the communist state, and their influence was reduced through physical destruction or decades of neglect.

Now we see something similar in Tbilisi. Georgia's political leadership is destroying a symbol that, for many, recalls a time when the country clearly tied its future to Europe and Euro‑Atlantic ambitions — an era full of ambition, openness, and a desire to belong to the European cultural sphere.

The Rike Park pipes may have been liked or disliked. They were controversial, expensive, unfinished, politically charged — but they were symbolic. You cannot surgically remove eras from a society's memory once they have existed. Every such attempt reveals how insecure the present is.

World.title: Estonian seal-watching tour attracts the animals with classical music
World.content:
Seal-watching trips off Estonia's northern coast are giving visitors a close-up look at the Baltic Sea's largest mammals, with classical music helping draw the curious animals closer to boats.

Boat captain Anti Nõmmela has been taking visitors on seal-watching trips along Estonia's northern coast for seven years.

"At least once a week, sometimes twice a week, and occasionally even more often. They're mainly around the Malusi islands. The conditions there are ideal for them. They can keep to themselves and the deep sea is right nearby. They can be there undisturbed," Nõmmela said, adding that, in his view, Estonia may even have too many seals. He has seen around 40 at one time.

Visitors on seal-watching trips need not worry about coming away disappointed without seeing a single marine animal. There is a secret trick for attracting the seals: playing them classical music.

Epp Libe, a guide with Prangli Reisid, confirmed that seals really do swim closer to the boat when classical music is played.

"The rhythms and harmonies in classical music are calm and flowing. Seals are also very curious, and because it's not a natural sound in the marine environment, it draws them in," Libe said.

Legend has it that in 1894, brothers Aleksander and Gustav Aksberg, who lived on Aksi Island, were sailing home from Oulu when they decided to play the violin and harmonium aboard their boat.

"At one point, they heard this pleasant snorting sound coming from the stern. They looked and saw that seals had gathered and were following them. That's how the connection was made that perhaps classical music could be the key," Libe said.

The sea was fairly windy for seal watching on Sunday, but the trip still provided participants with plenty of excitement.

"It was really nice. The waves were fun. We got splashed with a little seawater, so that was refreshing. It was also exciting to see seals in real life rather than at a zoo. At first they were a little farther away, but later we got closer with the boat. They're these cute, chubby pups. I'd take a couple home with me right away," Jevgeni said.

The Malusi Islands are home to Harju County's largest seal habitat. The sunnier and calmer the weather, the better the chances of seeing seals.

"Once we had perfect beach weather — the sea was as smooth as a mirror. Just imagine it: We want to go to the beach in weather like that too. There were more than 30 of them on the rocks, while the rest were splashing around in the water and climbing in and out," Libe said.

Seen from a boat, seals look small, cute and soft. In reality, the gray seal is the largest mammal in the Baltic Sea. Males can weigh up to 300 kilograms (660 pounds) and grow to more than 2 meters (6.6 feet) in length.

World.title: Estonian national team players make mark for clubs against West Ham, Celtic
World.content:
Europe's top football leagues are returning to their regular seasons as summer nears its end, and three Estonian national team players have already been involved in the action.

Rocco Robert Shein impresses for Portsmouth

Two players in particular were on form for U.K. clubs, in one case scoring a goal, but ultimately were disappointed with their results.

Midfielder Rocco Robert Shein had a good match for his new club Portsmouth F.C. of the English second tier, the EFL Championship.

Shein, 23, was making his competitive debut on Saturday for Pompey and played the full 90 minutes in front of more than 50,000 spectators at the London Olympic Stadium against the newly relegated West Ham United – though the game was a League Cup. Clash.

Midfielder Adrian Segecic put Portsmouth ahead in the 33rd minute, but successive strikes from Valentin Castellanos and Jarrod Bowen gave the Hammers a 2-1 lead at half-time.

Five minutes into the second half, capped twice by Argentina scored again and so it remained with West Ham winning 3-1.

The Estonian, who delivered some dangerous corners into the opposition penalty area and forced the West Ham 'keeper into a save with a long-range effort, came in for some praise from BBC pundits after the match.

Portsmouth's first EFL Championship match of the season is this coming Saturday, at home to QPR.

Rocco Robert Shein Source: Portsmouth FC

Schjønning-Larsen nets one against Celtic

Meanwhile north of the border left-back Michael Schjønning-Larsen put one home against reigning Scottish Premiership champions Celtic, though this was somewhat of a consolation goal as his team, Kilmarnock, went down 5–1 at home against the Bhoys.

The hosts struggled in the first half to contain Danish striker Kasper Högh, who scored Celtic's opener in the 2nd minute, found the net again in the 33rd minute, and completed a hat-trick two minutes later.

Then at the start of the second half, the visitors scored again via another Scandinavian, Swedish winger Benjamin Nygren. Schjønning-Larsen's consolation goal for the hosts came in the 56th minute, but Celtic responded with another goal from Luke McCowan in the 75th minute.

The Estonian had been taken off a minute earlier.

After two matches in the regular season, Killie have zero points after losing their opening game 4–3 away to St. Johnstone as well. They and Schjønning-Larsen next face Hibernian.

Paskotši helps Gent open league season with win

While he did not score, Estonia defender Maksim Paskotši at least tasted victory at the weekend as his team Gent opened the Belgian top flight league season with a 2-0 home win over Mechelen.

Maksim Paskotši. Source: KAA Gent/Facebook

Paskotši, who had just returned from a long injury layoff, came on as a substitute at the start of the second half.

Both of Gent's goals came at the end of the first half thanks to Portuguese full-back Tiago Araujo and Panamanian striker Josue Vergara scored the second.

Gent next play at home to Swedish side IFK Göteborg in the UEFA Conference League qualifier second leg with a one goal. Gent won 1-0 in the first leg away and so have an away goal advantage.

World.title: MP: Estonia has a top public servant competition instead of presidential elections
World.content:
Newly independent MP Meelis Kiili told ERR that while he respects Ülle Madise as justice chancellor, he cannot support her as a presidential candidate until he hears her views on foreign policy, national defense and social policy.

"We don't have a presidential election; we have a competition for a top public office. An election requires at least two candidates and a debate, but we don't have that right now," Kiili told ERR.

He added that he has great respect for Ülle Madise both as a person and as a legal expert, but that does not mean he would vote for her on that basis alone. Kiili said he does not know Madise's positions on her role as supreme commander of national defense, or on foreign policy, social policy and other issues.

Regarding his departure from the Reform Party, Kiili said he made the decision a week and a half ago.

"My own reflection told me that we no longer have any common ground. I continue to support a liberal economy, but we disagree on the issue of the nation-state and particularly on matters concerning national defense," he said.

Kiili said he cannot currently say whether he plans to join another political party or whether he will run in the next Riigikogu elections.

"One thing at a time. So far, I have tried to work across party lines. If I can continue working in national defense and security, then I may continue in politics. If not, I don't have to."

Asked what will happen to the National Defense Committee now that both he and committee chair Kalev Stoicescu have left parties in the governing coalition, Kiili said they would have to wait until the committee meets. According to Kiili, the National Defense Committee is unusual in that votes do not fall along coalition and opposition lines.

"Decisions there were based on expertise and the stronger argument," he said.

Kiili, who until now had been a member of the Reform Party, announced Monday that he had decided to leave the party and continue serving in the Riigikogu as an unaffiliated MP.

World.title: Estonia's ruling coalition loses majority after 2 MPs quit parties
World.content:
Estonia's two-party governing coalition lost its majority on Monday after two members of parliament resigned from their respective parties, reducing the number of seats to 50 of 101.

Eesti 200's Kalev Stoicescu and Reform's Meelis Kiili separately announced they were leaving their parties. Stoicescu made the announcement on social media on Sunday evening, while Kiili did so on Monday morning.

Kalev Stoicescu

According to Stoicescu, the decision had been a long time coming and he had considered whether he wanted to remain in politics at all.

"I stepped down from the party's board back in February 2024. I did not run in the local elections in October 2025. I thought for a long time about whether to continue in politics at all. People close to me and voters have unanimously encouraged me to continue and run in the next Riigikogu elections. I trust myself and the people close to me," the politician said.

Stoicescu also said he has already received offers to join other parties but has not yet made a decision.

"I want to continue contributing to Estonia's future, particularly in the areas of defense, security and foreign policy," Stoicescu said.

Meelis Kiili

"This is not a decision made on the spur of the moment. I have arrived at it over a longer period of time, primarily because my views on Estonia's national defense and security and their long-term development have increasingly diverged from the party's political choices," he said, explaining his decision.

Kiili said he does not regret joining the Reform Party.

"I have met many good people in the Reform Party and made good acquaintances and friends. I am grateful for that. But in politics, there comes a point when you have to ask yourself whether belonging to a party helps you stand up for the principles that brought you into politics or whether it begins to constrain you. For me, the answer to that question is now clear.

Meelis Kiili. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

"That is why the Reform Party and I are going our separate ways."

"I will continue in the Riigikogu as an unaffiliated MP and will keep working on issues where my knowledge and experience can benefit Estonia."

Meelis Kiili joined the Reform Party ahead of the last Riigikogu elections, on November 2, 2022. He ran in Ida-Viru County, received 1,289 votes and was elected.

Following Kiili's departure from the Reform Party and its parliamentary group, as well as Kalev Stoicescu's announcement a day earlier that he was leaving Eesti 200, the governing coalition now has 50 MPs in parliament, effectively making it a minority government.

Stoicescu associated with Parempoolsed

Stoicescu himself said he intends to run in the next Riigikogu elections and has already received offers to join other parties.

ERR has been told that Stoicescu is most likely to join the nonparliamentary Parempoolsed (Right-wingers) ahead of the Riigikogu elections. Polling firms Emor, Norstat and Turu-uuringud currently put the party's support at 6–7 percent. Parempoolsed have struggled with a lack of well-known figures and Stoicescu joining would certainly help them.

It will also be interesting to see how Stoicescu's departure from Eesti 200 affects the dynamics of the Riigikogu's committees, particularly the National Defense Committee, which Stoicescu currently chairs. The National Defense Committee has 11 members, and before Stoicescu left Eesti 200, the governing coalition held a narrow six-member majority.

The next Riigikogu elections will take place March 7, 2027, seven months from now.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) and Eesti 200 head Kristina Kallas. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

World.title: Tartu Old Town bar owners concerned about residential development
World.content:
Several bars in Tartu's Old Town are concerned about apartments due to be completed in the heart of the city in a few years and potential conflicts with the new residents who will move into them.

The building on the corner of Gildi and Rüütli streets in Tartu's Old Town, built in 1838, has served as a broadcloth factory, a girls' school and a polyclinic. Now, after standing empty for several years, the building is being converted into office space and 53 apartments, mostly one- and two-room units. Nearby bars are concerned about their potential new neighbors, fearing noise complaints and conflicts similar to those surrounding Genialistide Klubi, which Tartu has been trying to resolve for the past year and a half.

"Rüütli tänav is Tartu's main downtown street. This is where the nightlife is most concentrated. We already have noise problems, which have been discussed extensively in Tartu, so how do you resolve a situation where short-term rental apartments are allowed on the main downtown street, which is the center of nightlife? Why are short-term rental apartments allowed on this street? It's clear from the outset that there are going to be problems here and experience so far has shown that I have to resolve all these problems out of my own pocket, with my own money, nerves and everything else," Kivi bar owner Karin Kiplok said.

Jaan Tover, who owns several bars near the new apartments, said they are also concerned because the city is not taking steps to prevent problems related to nightlife. When problems arise, businesses on Rüütli tänav are left to resolve them themselves. The developer said its plans have taken the location into account.

"These are mostly smaller homes that will probably attract younger people without children who may be less bothered by the associated disturbance. The other thing is that, from a construction standpoint, we have to take great care to make sure the windows are very well insulated. Also, there won't be any ventilation openings in the wall," said Kaarel Kiidron, managing partner at developer Livida.

Although prospective apartment buyers are informed about the bustle on Rüütli tänav, some residents who expected noise and people on the street have encountered issues they did not anticipate.

"The vibration that comes through the window on weekends is actually pretty bad, and it's specifically from the music. I knew there would be noise, but I didn't expect the vibration to come through the walls of the building. It's coming through from the building next door. I knew there would be a lot of people here, and people don't bother me, but there could be less music here," said Triin Varul, a Rüütli tänav resident.

Tartu's Rüütli tänav. Source: Airika Harrik/ERR

Tartu Deputy Mayor Kertu Vuks said the city's vision is for the Old Town to accommodate both housing and bars and cafes. If new Old Town residents encounter problems with noise, the city will address them on a case-by-case basis. At the same time, the city would like bars outside the Old Town to be viable as well.

"The city's hope and vision is also for other locations — not just Rüütli tänav — and neighborhood bars to be viable," Vuks said. She added that, ultimately, bars will not have to leave Rüütli tänav and businesses are free to choose the locations that suit them best.
