World.title: Estonia axes unemployment benefit for young people finishing conscription
World.content:
New eligibility requirements mean that young graduates cannot receive unemployment benefits after finishing school or completing military service, unless they have previously worked for at least eight months.

A young person who goes straight from school into compulsory military service may be surprised to discover that, when looking for work after completing their service, they will have to rely on someone else for financial support because the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund will not pay them benefits. The exception is if they managed to work enough while still in school.

Previously, both school graduates and young people completing military service were eligible for unemployment allowance, but that form of support ceased to exist at the beginning of this year. Unemployment insurance benefits are now available, with eligibility depending on a person's previous participation in the labor market, said Kirsti Melesk, head of the employment department at the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications.

"As with any other type of insurance, the system works so that a person becomes entitled to benefits if they have contributed to the insurance system and the insured event then occurs. In the case of unemployment insurance, that means becoming unemployed. The same principle can be compared with home or auto insurance: If a person has never paid insurance premiums, they cannot claim an insurance payout when an insured event occurs. The purpose of unemployment insurance benefits is to partially replace income previously earned from employment during the period when a person is looking for work, rather than directly guaranteeing an income to everyone who is out of work, including those who did not previously have such an income," Melesk said.

She said conscripts are in the same position as school graduates who also have no previous work experience when they begin looking for work after graduation and have to manage without financial support from the state. Young people can nevertheless register as unemployed and make use of services designed to help them find work.

"We currently have no plans to create any kind of exemption for conscripts. Instead, we consider it important to support young people in their job searches, helping them gain their first work experience and get a foot in the door of the labor market. Since the beginning of this year, for example, the Unemployment Insurance Fund has also had youth counselors who specialize specifically in supporting young people's job searches and providing them with counseling," Melesk said.

In certain cases, however, young school graduates may still be eligible for unemployment insurance benefits if they managed to work while attending school. To qualify, they must have worked during at least eight months over the preceding three years, for at least one day in each of those months.

"A person must have accumulated at least eight months of unemployment insurance coverage. This can be accrued, for example, through employment under an employment contract, and if a person has worked under an employment contract for eight months, the requirement has already been met," said Vadim Djomin, head of unemployment insurance benefits at the Unemployment Insurance Fund. There are, however, exceptions.

"If a person works under a contract governed by the law of obligations, there must be eight payments from which unemployment insurance premiums have been withheld. In the case of employment contracts, a person must have worked for eight months and those months do not have to be consecutive. They can be under different contracts and in different months, but there must be at least eight months in total," Djomin said.

According to Djomin, a young person could accumulate the required eight months by working over three summers and would then be eligible for benefits from the Unemployment Insurance Fund after graduating.

Viru Infantry Battalian conscripts' passout, June 10. Source: mil.ee

The Estonian Defense Resources Agency has not discussed providing conscripts with financial support while they look for work after completing their service. If such support were introduced, it would have to come from the defense budget at the expense of specific military capabilities, the agency's director general, Anu Rannaveski, said.

"What is military service if not another form of training? Just as people study different fields at university, military service itself is training in national defense. Of course, as a society, we want to make it as easy as possible for young people to enter the labor market. I think military service itself already gives a young person a very strong competitive advantage. The studies we have conducted also show that, in the future, young people who have completed military service earn more than those who have not," Rannaveski said.

She said the trend in recent years also shows that a significant number of young people remain in the Estonian Defense Forces as active-duty personnel after completing their military service. They account for around 7.5 percent of conscripts.

World.title: Asian stocks track Wall St higher after US job losses ease rate fears
World.content:
Hong Kong – Stocks rose Monday as investors pared their bets on a US interest rate hike after data showed thousands of jobs were lost in July, though sentiment was dented by another spike in oil prices as hopes for an end to the Middle East crisis fade.

Tech firms enjoyed a fresh bout of buying following a volatile run in recent weeks, with Japanese and Korean chipmakers leading the charge.

The positive mood was fuelled by figures from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics that showed 23,000 jobs were lost last month, while growth in May and June was revised down.

The reading suggested the world’s number one economy was slowing, though traders welcomed the prospect the Federal Reserve will hold off hiking borrowing costs for the time being.

The chances of an increase in September were slashed to about 43 percent from 64 percent a week ago, according to Bloomberg.

Inflation data due later this week will be the next guide for investors.

The news helped Wall Street higher, with the S&P 500 ending at a fresh record high, while tech firms — which benefit from lower rates — helped the Nasdaq pile on more than one percent.

And the gains filtered through to Asia, with Tokyo climbing two percent thanks to healthy advances for Kioxia, Tokyo Electron and Advantest. Seoul was also up as chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung rallied.

Hong Kong, Taipei, Shanghai, Wellington and Jakarta were also up.

“Markets treated the report as a meaningful challenge to near term Fed rate hike expectations, effectively concluding the Fed has time on its side,” wrote National Australia Bank’s Rodrigo Catril.

But he added: “The report reduces the case that the labour market is adding inflation pressures, but it does not provide a clean green light for a dovish pivot.

“The report is unlikely, by itself, to deter a September hike… inflation remains the more pressing side of the mandate. The next (consumer price index) prints (for July and August) ahead of the September Federal Open Market Committee meeting are the key data releases to watch.”

The dollar clawed back the losses suffered Friday in reaction to the jobs figures, and continued to gain against the yen after plunging earlier this month when US and Japanese authorities embarked on a historic joint intervention to support the Japanese unit.

Crude prices jumped around one percent to extend gains at the end of last week as Iran’s Revolutionary Guards insisted Sunday that they would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the United States complied with a list of demands.

Tehran insists on retaining control of the waterway — through which a fifth of world oil and LNG pass — after the war and wants to charge tolls for passage, which Washington has pushed back against.

Attacks in the strait, which was free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire, and mediators have urged both sides to return to the terms of a subsequent June memorandum that set out a path for peace talks.

Iran on Saturday released a list of conditions for reopening the strait, including an end to the war on all fronts, the lifting of a US counterblockade of Iranian ports, the end of sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage, the Tasnim news agency reported.

Those conditions echoed the terms of the June agreement, which included a provision to create a $300 billion reconstruction fund for Iran.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday that their strategy was to maintain their blockade “until the enemy accepts all our conditions… the strait is now actually a theatre of war for us and not just a waterway”.

For his part, US President Donald Trump said in an interview: “We are low-keying it.”

“We are only semi-negotiating with them,” he was quoted as saying. “We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money.”

“It will work out,” he added. “It’s like a chess game.”

World.title: NBA champion player and historic coach Nelson dead at 86
World.content:
San Francisco – Don Nelson, who won the second-most games of any coach in NBA history and five NBA titles as a player with the Boston Celtics, died on Sunday, his family announced. He was 86.

Nelson was a member of NBA championship teams with Boston from 1966 to 1976 and the Celtics retired his jersey number 19.

As a coach, Nelson finished with a record of 1,335-1,063 — what had been an NBA record until Gregg Popovich passed him in 2022 — in stints with Golden State, Milwaukee, New York and Dallas from 1976 to 2010.

“Don Nelson revolutionized NBA basketball through his fearlessness, ingenuity and deep conviction,” NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement.

“He spent nearly 50 years in the NBA -– winning five championships as a player with the Boston Celtics before building one of the most successful and pioneering coaching careers in league history.

“He brought an unmistakable personality to everything he did, and his impact on our sport will continue to be felt for generations.”

Nelson, who was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2012, never reached the NBA Finals as a coach but was remembered as a historic figure among bench bosses.

“The Golden State Warriors mourn the passing of Hall of Fame head coach Don Nelson,” the team said in a statement.

“‘Nellie’ was one of the most innovative and influential coaches in NBA history and an iconic figure in Warriors history…

“More than anything, Don Nelson will be remembered for his authenticity, larger-than-life personality, and incredible passion for basketball and his influence on the Warriors franchise will endure for years to come.”

Steve Kerr, the current Warriors coach, recalled Nelson as a visionary whose influence remains with the modern era of the league.

“Don Nelson was a true innovator whose influence on the game of basketball is still felt today,” Kerr said.

“He consistently challenged conventional thinking, experimented with different lineups and styles of play, and saw possibilities in the game that others often did not.

“So much of what is now commonplace in the modern NBA can be traced back to the way Nellie approached the game.”

The Celtics paid tribute to Nelson’s playing career in a statement.

“Nellie was a tough and reliable all-around player whose tenacity and ability to ‘think the game’ was on full display throughout his 11 seasons with the Boston Celtics, where he was a key member of five championship teams across two eras,” the Celtics said.

The Bucks paid tribute to Nelson’s first NBA coaching stint.

“During his 11 seasons as Bucks coach from 1976-1987, Nellie won two of his three NBA Coach of the Year awards and established himself as one of the most innovative and visionary leaders in basketball history,” the Bucks said.

The Dallas Mavericks called him an innovator and legend whose “impact will never be forgotten,” saying he left “an incredible mark on our franchise and the game of basketball.”

World.title: Zambia vote to test Hichilema’s economic record
World.content:
Lusaka – Zambians vote Thursday in a closely watched presidential election that will test whether recent economic gains can offset frustration over the high cost of living in one of Africa’s most stable democracies.

Incumbent Hakainde Hichilema faces Brian Mundubile, a former ally of late president Edgar Lungu, who surged to the front of a fragmented opposition after being backed by a coalition of rival parties.

Up to 8.7 million voters — a majority of them women — will decide whether Hichilema’s economic reforms deserve another term or whether the opposition can turn widespread discontent into a comeback.

Hichilema, leader of the United Party for National Development (UPND), won the presidency in 2021 on his sixth attempt, inheriting a country in sovereign default after years of heavy borrowing under Lungu.

His victory marked a rare peaceful transfer of power to an opposition party through the ballot box in Africa.

The government has since secured a landmark debt restructuring agreement, restored an International Monetary Fund programme and returned the economy to growth, winning praise from international lenders and investors.

But many Zambians say the benefits have been slow to reach ordinary citizens. Rising food prices, unemployment and persistent poverty remain dominant concerns in a country where more than 70 percent of the population lives on less than three dollars a day, according to World Bank data.

“Worldwide there has been recognition that we are doing well but he needs to bring it home,” medical student Semi Malama, 26, told AFP.

Zambia is Africa’s second-largest copper producer and the government has set an ambitious target of tripling production by 2031.

Chinese companies are major players in the mining sector, underscoring Beijing’s outsized economic influence in the country.

– Continuity vs change –

The opposition has sought to exploit the squeeze on household finances, arguing that reforms have failed to improve livelihoods despite signs of recovery.

Until the opposition coalesced behind Mundubile, re-election had looked all but certain for the 64-year-old Hichilema, widely known as “HH”.

Although 14 candidates are on the ballot, analysts say the race has narrowed into a two-horse contest between Hichilema and Mundubile, a 55-year-old former minister.

“The opposition alliance is bringing energy to their rallies and appealing to youth, women, and rural voters,” Joseph Siegle, director of research at the Africa Center for Strategic Studies, told AFP.

Mundubile’s challenge is built around “mopping up” the support base of Lungu’s Patriotic Front, particularly in the north and east, where the former ruling party has historically held sway, political analyst Louw Nel said.

But his relatively late entry into the race and association with the Lungu era could limit his ability to expand beyond that base, he said.

Nearly half of registered voters are aged between 18 and 35, making young people a potentially pivotal bloc.

“Ultimately, the election will hinge on whether voters believe continuity offers the best chance of consolidating recent economic reforms, or whether they conclude that change is needed to address immediate economic pressures,” Institute for Security Studies researcher Zenge Simakoloyi told AFP.

– Tensions –

The campaign has been marked by pockets of violence and allegations of intimidation.

Police have used tear gas to disperse clashes between rival supporters, while Mundubile’s National Republican Party (NRPUP) has accused authorities of restricting its campaign activities.

The opposition leader last week alleged that snipers were deployed at a campaign event in Mongu, about 580 kilometres (360 miles) west of Lusaka, calling the tear gas “just the tip of the iceberg.”

Polling stations open Thursday at 0600 local time (0400 GMT) and close 12 hours later.

Zambians will also elect an expanded parliament, with directly elected members of parliament rising to 226 from 156.

Presidential results are due August 17, according to the electoral commission’s calendar. A candidate needs more than 50 percent of valid votes to win outright; otherwise, the top contenders face a run-off.

The outcome could hinge on “relatively small swings” in support across Zambia’s 10 provinces, Simakoloyi said.

The vote will also test Zambia’s reputation for political stability amid growing concerns over restrictions on dissent and a narrowing political space.

World.title: No mercy for corrupt officials as Al-Zaidi widens Iraq crackdown
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s anti-corruption effort has shown no signs of stopping, with arrests and investigations ranging from senior Oil Ministry officials to MPs, former provincial leaders, and other government figures since he assumed office.

One of the main early instances involved Adnan Al-Jumaili, the former deputy oil minister for refining affairs, whose imprisonment was a key development in the probe.

Statements gathered from Al-Jumaili assisted authorities in expanding their investigation into a larger network of politicians and officials accused of profiting from government contracts and state resources.

That probe culminated in a spectacular operation on June 28, when Iraqi security forces blocked off access to Baghdad’s highly defended Green Zone and conducted coordinated raids on political and government heavyweights.

Iraq’s national news agency first claimed 47 arrests, including 12 current parliamentarians, a former legislator, a former aide to former Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, and a top Oil Ministry official.

According to sources inside Iraq’s anti-corruption authorities, there were 67 people held during the first phase of the “Dawn Crackdown”.

Ali Maarij, Iraq’s Deputy Oil Minister for distribution and another key player in the country’s energy industry, was among those held.

According to prosecutors, the larger investigation turned up claims of the misuse of public resources, government contracts, and commissions for personal or political gain.

Authorities also recovered a considerable quantity of assets related to the investigations. Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council said in July that 375 kg of gold had been confiscated as part of the al-Jumaili probe, with more cash and gold found in subsequent operations.

Instead of finishing with the first Green Zone attacks, the campaign lasted all of July.

Between July 20 and July 26, Iraqi police apprehended 31 persons in seven corruption cases, reflecting the government’s escalating enforcement campaign.

So far, August has delivered a slew of high-profile cases.

Former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, was held as authorities investigated claims involving public finances, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court for a separate inquiry.

On Sunday, police detained Hashem al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company, on suspicion of corruption regarding a Ministry of Defense contract.

The specifics of the alleged infractions and the contract’s worth have not yet been released.

The financial impact of the crackdown is becoming significant.

The Eco Iraq Observatory said on Sunday that police had recovered around 482.6 billion Iraqi dinars ($371.6 million) in stolen assets, including cash and gold.

Taken together, the arrests convey an increasingly clear message from Al-Zaidi’s government: senior political ties, legislative standing, or positions inside major ministries should not exclude people from scrutiny.

However, arrests alone will not decide whether Iraq eventually succeeds in combating corruption.

Success will be predicated on transforming the present campaign into long-term institutional transformation via open government contracts, improved audits, digital financial systems, independent investigations, and tighter controls over public funds.

This is especially crucial as Iraq pursues tens of billions of dollars in foreign investment and works to strengthen economic ties with the United States, Europe, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and other Gulf nations.

Investors need to be confident that predictable rules govern contracts and public institutions rather than political interference.

The crackdown has also received backing from key international partners.

During a phone call with French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday, Macron reaffirmed France’s support for Iraq’s anti-corruption drive and economic reforms, as well as continued cooperation on counterterrorism and strengthening the capabilities of the Iraqi armed forces.

But the problem goes beyond financial corruption.

Al-Zaidi has committed to reinforce state power and bring armaments under government control, adding to the administration’s already arduous task of dealing with entrenched political and economic interests.

Iraq’s long-term goal must consequently be greater than capturing people.

Baghdad needs institutions strong enough to prevent corruption and foreign intervention from resurfacing under new political networks, whether sponsored by Iran or another external entity.

If Al-Zaidi can combine rigorous enforcement with due process and institutional change, the campaign might greatly boost trust in the Iraqi government.

Without such institutional improvements, even hundreds of arrests risk becoming a momentary crackdown rather than the long-term transformation Iraq requires.

World.title: Iraq opens its first IMAX cinema in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated its first IMAX theater at the Iraq Mall in Baghdad, introducing the premium large-screen movie format to the nation for the first time.

Sarwa Abdul Wahid, the Acting Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities, formally opened the new Iraqi Cinema branch in the mall, adding to Baghdad’s fast expanding entertainment and leisure sector.

According to IMAX’s official listing, the Iraq Mall site in Baghdad has an IMAX with Laser auditorium and stadium seating.

The launch allows Iraqi consumers to see important worldwide movies in IMAX without having to fly abroad, like Christopher Nolan’s 2026 blockbuster The Odyssey.

The film, starring Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, Robert Pattinson, and Lupita Nyong’o, was the first feature film filmed exclusively on IMAX film cameras.

The Odyssey has also emerged as one of 2026’s greatest box office triumphs, earning more over $260 million globally in its first weekend.

Iraqi Cinema is now offering daily IMAX screenings of the film at its Iraq Mall location.

IMAX brings another worldwide entertainment option to Baghdad, as Iraq seeks additional investment in retail malls, restaurants, hotels, theaters, and other leisure developments, while also growing its domestic tourist and entertainment sectors.

World.title: Iraq arrests senior Trade Ministry official Hashem Al-Sudani
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi prosecutors detained Hashem Al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company (GAMCO), on Sunday for suspected embezzlement in a contract with the Ministry of Defense.

The contract’s specifics, including its value and the particular alleged infractions under investigation, have not been released. Al-Sudani’s arrest is part of Iraq’s growing anti-corruption effort, which targets prominent government officials, legislators, and business leaders.

The new arrest comes as Baghdad ramps up the “Dawn Crackdown,” an anti-corruption operation that began on June 28 by Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to probe big crimes involving public contracts and state finances.

The initiative has gained traction among senior and politically connected individuals.

Recently, police arrested former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court as part of a separate inquiry.

Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and reclaiming public monies, with authorities attempting to show that probes would extend to officials regardless of party or institutional affiliation.

Corruption has long been a major impediment to Iraq’s growth, depleting state resources, degrading public services, and deterring private and international investment.

The ongoing arrests imply Baghdad’s new effort is spreading to official institutions, but anyone arrested or interrogated has not been convicted and is still subject to due process.

World.title: Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian strikes killed two people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight Saturday and Sunday, while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia’s Belgorod region.

The World Health Organization denounced a strike that destroyed a warehouse in Ukraine holding medical supplies.

More than four years after the start of Russia’s large-scale offensive against Ukraine, both countries are ramping up long-range strikes. The resulting civilian casualties led the United Nations to condemn both sides last week.

Russia is relying on “ballistic terror,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday on social media, stating that 61 missiles of various types had been fired at Ukraine this week.

“More pressure, more sanctions against Russia and more air defence for Ukraine are needed,” he added.

The two people killed by a Russian drone strike were in the major northeastern city of Kharkiv, where four floors of a residential building were also destroyed, said Zelensky.

Twenty-three people were also wounded, according to regional governor Oleg Synegoubov, sharing images of a gutted building with emergency services working at the scene.

Zelensky said eight people had also been wounded overnight in Odesa, where strikes damaged the power grid, the port, and residential buildings.

He condemned another “absolutely brutal” strike targeting energy infrastructure near a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, in the Dnipropetrovsk region that wounded nine people, including four children.

– WHO condemns warehouse strike –

World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said a WHO warehouse stocking medical supplies in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro had been destroyed in strikes on Friday.

“I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care MUST STOP. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare,” Tedros in a post on X Sunday.

“Even wars have rules. One of those is that health must be protected!”

In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack on the border city of Belgorod killed three people, according to the region’s acting governor, Alexander Shuvaev.

Twenty-five people, including children aged four and nine, were also wounded, he added.

Fires broke out in cars, two apartment buildings, and a house, said Shuvaev.

A video released by Russian media shows an apartment building engulfed in flames at night, watched by residents gathered across the street.

On the front line, the Russian army said Sunday they had captured two small villages in Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region. The claim has not yet been independently verified.

One of them, Vasiutynske, is about 10 kilometres (six miles) from the city of Kramatorsk, a Ukrainian urban and logistical hub.

– Zelensky defends strikes –

Zelensky, in his evening address on Sunday, defended Ukraine’s responses to Russia’s attacks — including strikes on oil refineries, air-defence systems and radar stations — as “truly just responses”.

“The Russian war will be increasingly felt at home, in Russia,” he said.

On Thursday, United Nations chief Antonio Guterres condemned both sides for their repeated attacks on civilian areas.

“Attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are a clear violation of international humanitarian law, and must stop immediately,” he said.

The Russian invasion, which began four and a half years ago, continues with prospects of a peace agreement largely stalled.

World.title: Como sign England defender Chalobah from Chelsea
World.content:
Milan – Como have completed the signing of England centre-back Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea for a reported fee of 30 million euros ($34.5 million), the Serie A club announced Sunday.

The 27-year-old has penned a five-year deal with Cesc Fabregas’s ambitious side, who will play in the Champions League for the first time this season.

“I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans,” said Chalobah, who made 151 appearances for Chelsea.

“I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together.”

Como pipped AC Milan and Juventus to Italy’s fourth and final Champions League place last season.

Scudetto holders Inter Milan had also been heavily linked with a move for Chalobah, before reportedly deciding the asking price was too high.

“Trevoh is an important signing for us and a player who represents the level of ambition we have at this club,” said Como coach Fabregas, a former Chelsea midfielder.

“He is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”

Chalobah was part of the England squad which finished third at the World Cup last month, after receiving a late call-up as a replacement for the injured Tino Livramento.

He could make his Como debut when they visit Udinese in their Serie A opener on August 22.

World.title: Uttarakhand Forward 2.0 | Prasanna Kumar Patro lays out Uttarakhand’s ecotourism roadmap
World.content:
Uttarakhand Forward 2.0 is the second edition of The Times of India's flagship video series spotlighting the state's journey of growth, innovation and transformative governance.

Through exclusive conversations with policymakers, administrators, industry leaders, educationists and experts, the series explores the ideas, initiatives and vision shaping Uttarakhand's future across infrastructure, clean energy, education, tourism, sustainability and more. The campaign highlights the policies driving progress, the challenges and opportunities ahead, and the roadmap for the state's next phase of development.

Can tourism and conservation go hand in hand?

As Uttarakhand balances growing tourism with the need to protect its rich forests and wildlife, the conversation around sustainable development has never been more important.

In this episode of Uttarakhand Forward 2.0, Richa Jain Kalra speaks with Prasanna Kumar Patro, MD, Ecotourism Development Corporation, CCF Ecotourism & CCF (HRD), Department of Forest, Government of Uttarakhand, about the state's vision for preserving its natural heritage while creating sustainable livelihoods.





The discussion explores ecotourism, forest conservation, human-wildlife conflict, climate change, forest fires, biodiversity, community participation through Van Panchayats, and the role of local communities in protecting Uttarakhand's ecosystems.

From mass tourism to value tourism

World.title: ED launches probe into Jharkhand recruitment exams amid student protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has launched a probe into irregularities in several recruitment exams in Jharkhand, including the JSSC-CGL exam, as news agency PTI quoted officials saying on Monday.

The agency has taken note of an FIR filed by the state police CID and other complaints and will investigate the matter under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).

The development comes as students have been protesting for 16 days, demanding a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment exams, particularly the JSSC-CGL (Jharkhand General Graduate Level Combined Competitive Examination).

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The protests in Jharkhand has entered its 17th day on Monday.

The students have refused to end their protest. The agitated students have started their march to "ghero" assembly, despite the government claiming it has accepted "98 per cent of the demands".

However, the protesters has rejected Hemant Soren-led government's claims of "98% demands met," saying that only "3 out of 13 exams were cancelled."

Meanwhile, the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) saw a major change on Sunday, with all three of its members resigning. The members are Ajeeta Bhattacharya, wife of JMM leader Supriyo Bhattacharyya, Anima Hansda and Jamal Ahmad.

Their resignations came after the Jharkhand CID summoned them for questioning over alleged irregularities, including paper leaks.

World.title: 'Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother': Vijay moves Tamil anthem resolution; DMK, AIADMK back it
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday moved a government resolution in the assembly making the rendition of Tamil Thai Vazhthu, the state song, mandatory at the beginning of official programmes across the state.

Moving the resolution in the state assembly, Vijay said his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's linguistic and cultural rights and urged legislators to set aside political differences in supporting the measure.

"Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother," Vijay said in an emotive speech, adding that, "Tamil is not only a language but also our life and emotions."

"Tamil means pride, Tamil means power. The moment you say 'Tamil', the entire Tamil Nadu will come together and stand as one," he said.

"Tamil Thai Vazhthu must hold the first place in Tamil Nadu. Giving first place to Tamil Thaai Vaazhthu is our state right," he noted.

"Saying that Tamil Thai Vazhthu should be sung first does not need to become a political debate," the Tamil nadu CM said, appealing to members across party lines to support the resolution.

Under the resolution, Tamil Thai Vazhthu will be sung first at programmes held by educational institutions, universities, government offices, public sector undertakings and other public institutions in Tamil Nadu.





The resolution received support from both DMK and AIADMK legislators, with members backing the government's move to mandate the singing of the state song at official functions.

The move comes amid a recent advisory from the Union home ministry asking states and Union territories to comply with its January 28 directive on playing Vande Mataram before the National Anthem at official events.

It also comes against the backdrop of a July 9 communication from the ministry of home affairs regarding the singing of state songs at official programmes.

What does the resolution say?

The resolution describes Tamil Thai Vazhthu as an expression of respect for the Tamil language and culture and links its mandatory rendition to the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed under the Constitution.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Therefore, this House ( Tamil Nadu Assembly ) emphasises that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" is an expression of respect for the Tamil language and Tamil culture. In accordance with the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed by the Constitution of India, and with a view to preserving the Cultural identity of Tamil Nadu, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly unanimously resolves that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" shall be mandatorily sung first, before the commencement of programmes held by all Educational Institutions, Universities, Government Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and other Public Institutions in Tamil Nadu," the resolution said.

The resolution also notes that Tamil is one of the world's oldest classical languages and describes Tamil civilisation as one of the world's oldest cultural traditions.

Tamil Nadu had first directed that Tamil Thai Vazhthu be sung at the beginning of official functions through a government order issued on November 23, 1970.

The state government formally accorded the song the status of the state song on December 12, 2021, making its rendition mandatory at official programmes and institutions across the state.

World.title: Jharkhand assembly gherao: Security stepped up with 750m curbs, barbed-wire barricades
World.content:
Jharkhand Police imposed prohibitory orders around the Assembly and strengthened security across the city as students marched against alleged recruitment exam irregularities.

March to begin at 10:30 am

Prohibitory orders around Assembly

Barricades and barbed wire deployed

Security stepped up across Ranchi

Schools to remain closed

Ranchi administration warns against aggressive protests

BJP alleges Aditya Sahu placed under house arrest

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Jamshedpur also under restrictions

Students allege police stopping protesters from reaching Ranchi

Students asked to maintain peace

Police clarifies viral âpellet gunâ video

NEW DELHI: Ranchi is under heightened security on Monday as protesting students prepare to march to the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The students, who have been agitating for 16 days, have announced a âVidhan Sabha Marchâ despite the state government saying it has accepted 98 per cent of their demands.The march is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am, with students gathering at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium from 9 am, according to student leader Ravindra Paswan. He urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms.Speaking to ANI, Paswan said, "A march to the Vidhan Sabha and a gherao will be conducted in a peaceful and constitutional manner. Students started gathering there at 9:00 AM. The march will commence between 10:30 and 11:00 AM. I urge all students and the general public to maintain peace and adhere to constitutional norms. Since we students are leading this movement, we must demonstrate that we are disciplined and educated. Students from every district of Jharkhand are arriving for today's protest; there will be a massive turnout."A prohibitory order has been imposed within a 750-metre radius of the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha from August 6 to 12.The restrictions will remain in force from 6 am to 10 pm each day.Police have put up barricades around the Assembly premises, with barbed wire installed at parts of the protest route to prevent demonstrators from reaching restricted areas.Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said that maintaining law and order during the march is everyoneâs responsibility. "We do not want a blot on the career of any student due to disruption of law and order. Barricades have been put in place at major points with the deployment of adequate police force across the city," the SSP said.The Jharkhand Police and district administration have made elaborate security arrangements across the city ahead of the studentsâ âVidhan Sabha Marchâ. The government said no student would be harassed during the protest.Most schools in Ranchi will remain closed on Monday in view of the planned march, with authorities taking precautionary measures ahead of the expected turnout.The Ranchi district administration appealed to agitating students to refrain from aggressive demonstrations and cautioned against violence or illegal activities during the march to the Assembly.BJP leader Amar Bauri alleged that the partyâs state unit president Aditya Sahu had been âput under house arrestâ ahead of Mondayâs protest.A prohibitory order was imposed in Jamshedpur from Sunday midnight in view of the protest march in Ranchi, according to an official statement.Protesters alleged that hundreds of students travelling to Ranchi from different parts of Jharkhand were being stopped by police forcefully.Student leader Ravindra Paswan urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms during the march, which is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana addressed concerns over a viral video that appeared to show a pellet gun, clarifying that the weapon was actually a paintball gun. "If a pellet gun is being carried, it is strictly for emergency situations. Regarding the viral video--what is being mistaken for a pellet gun is actually a paintball gun; it fires soft, colored balls used to mark and identify troublemakers. It is not a pellet gun," he was quoted by ANI as saying.

World.title: Sharad Pawar’s MPs to meet PM Modi; Congress asks them to delink women’s quota, delimitation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A delegation of eight MPs from Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) is scheduled to meet Prime Minister

on Monday during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.

Ahead of the meeting, the

has urged its alliance partner to convey the INDIA bloc's opposition to linking the implementation of women's reservation with the proposed delimitation exercise.

AICC secretary Sachin Sawant urged the NCP (SP) delegation to press Modi for the immediate implementation of the Women's Reservation Act, passed in 2023, without waiting for delimitation.

"It is learnt that the MPs of the Nationalist Congress Party - Sharadchandra Pawar will be meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday regarding issues concerning Maharashtra. We urge them to firmly convey to Prime Minister Modi that the INDIA Alliance's unequivocal position is that the Women's Reservation Act, passed in 2023, must be implemented immediately and should not be linked to delimitation," Sawant posted on X on Sunday.

"It is important that the unity of the INDIA Alliance and its opposition to the Modi government on this issue is made unequivocally clear," he added.

NCP (SP) MPs to raise Maharashtra issues

The Congress' appeal comes ahead of the meeting between

and eight NCP (SP) MPs, led by party MP Supriya Sule.

Sule had said on Saturday that the delegation would raise issues affecting Maharashtra, including farmer suicides, the water crisis and problems caused by rapid urbanisation.





"We - some MPs and I - were talking about that Prime Minister must be apprised about the problems in Maharashtra. There is water related issues, farmer suicides, and problems being faced due to urbanisation," Sule said at a press conference in Mumbai.

BJP leader Navneet Rana welcomed the proposed meeting, saying elected representatives should be able to raise issues concerning Maharashtra's development with the Prime Minister.

"I feel that if MPs from

Sharad Pawar

's party are meeting PM Modi for the sake of Maharashtra's development--driven by the belief that the state needs to progress further--then such a meeting is certainly not a bad thing," Rana said.

"While all sorts of speculations are being made, I believe any such speculation ultimately bodes well for Maharashtra; there could be nothing better than them approaching the PM to advocate for the state's development," she added.

The dispute centres on the government's proposed delimitation exercise and its connection with the implementation of the women's reservation law. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, proposed increasing the strength of the House to 850 seats and sought to expedite the implementation of the Women's Reservation Act passed in 2023.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The bill, however, failed to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting and was not passed during the extended Budget Session.

The Congress and other opposition parties have backed women's reservation but oppose making its implementation dependent on delimitation. They have argued that the reservation provisions should be implemented immediately rather than waiting for the expansion and redrawing of Lok Sabha constituencies.

World.title: India digest: TISS ex-student arrested after bail plea rejected; security guard rapes student on terrace
World.content:
TISS ex-student arrested after bail plea rejected

Hours after anticipatory bail applications of two former TISS students were rejected in a case stemming from an unauthorised campus event to pay homage to late Delhi University professor G N Saibaba last year, one of them, Abhirup Paul, 32, was arrested on Friday.

He was produced before a court on Saturday and sent to police custody till Monday.

Krishna image on WB House site sparks row

An image of Lord Krishna, accompanied by a religious-philosophical message, on the official website of Bengal legislative assembly sparked a political controversy, with Trinamool MLA Kunal Ghosh questioning whether imagery associated with a particular faith should appear on a govt institutionâs digital platform. Those browsing the website found, along with photos of CM Suvendu Adhikari and Speaker Rathindra Bose, an image of Lord Krishna with a message on the harmful effects of anger.

World.title: Protesting job aspirants face water cannons as they march to Jharkhand Assembly
World.content:
Thousands of job aspirants, protesting exam irregularities, faced water cannons as they marched to the Jharkhand assembly on Monday (August 11, 2026), breaching barricades one after the other.

Also read: Jharkhand students protest updates on August 10, 2026

Armed with tricolours and placards, the demonstrators broke into dance as police used water cannons when they reached the final barricade near Jagannathpur Temple on the road to the new Assembly Complex.

They raised slogans in support of their demands as their protest entered the 17th day.

The march, which coincided with the 51st birthday of Chief Minister Hemant Soren, began from outside the old Assembly building around 10:30 a.m.

JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a fast for nine days over the issue, joined the march in an ambulance despite losing 10.5 kg. He was seen carrying a portrait of former Chief Minister Shibu Soren.

“We are protesting peacefully, and we urge everyone to help us maintain that peace. We are raising the voice of lakhs of students who are fighting for their dreams and careers... My health is failing,” he said.

The placards being carried by the protesters read “Cancel JSSC-CGL Exams or Conduct a CBI Probe”, “Why is CID escaping from conducting a raid on JSSC?” and “Conduct an impartial investigation, bring out the truth.”

“If we cannot reach the assembly, our voices must reach them. We do not fear the government, which is treating us like traitors. We have been compelled to take to the streets,” a protester said.

The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, which is spearheading the agitation, said it has deployed around 500 volunteers to prevent anti-social elements from joining the march.

DSP Arvind Kumar Verma said the march has so far been peaceful, and police are exercising restraint.

Besides imposing prohibitory orders, heavy security has been deployed on the entire stretch, around 4 km long, with senior officers keeping a close watch, officials said.

More than 1,500 personnel from the Rapid Action Force, Indian Reserve Battalion, district police and QRT have been deployed, they said.

Most of the schools in the city have been closed, they added.

The Government has held several rounds of talks with the demonstrators but failed to break the deadlock. After the last round of deliberations, the government said it had accepted 98 per cent of the demands of the demonstrators.

However, the protesters said the government had agreed to cancel only three of the 13 exams they wanted scrapped.

“We will not compromise till our demand for a CBI probe is fulfilled,” JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch leader Ravindra Paswan said.

The agitators are demanding comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

They are also seeking cancellation of several recruitment tests, including the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination, and an independent probe into the alleged irregularities, either by the CBI or by a panel of retired high court judges from outside the state.

World.title: UDF-ruled panchayat in Malappuram seeks review of Kerala govt’s Priyadarshini free bus travel scheme
World.content:
The Othukkungal grama panchayat in Malappuram district, ruled by the United Democratic Front (UDF) constituent Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), has passed a resolution seeking to exclude women government employees from the Kerala government’s free KSRTC travel facility under the Priyadarshini scheme.

The resolution, moved by welfare standing committee chairperson Khamarudheen, welcomed the social benefits provided by the scheme but called for changes in its implementation.

Private services hit

It said the free travel scheme had adversely affected private bus services in the State, with operators facing a significant drop in passenger numbers.

The panchayat argued that women government employees with a regular income and other employment benefits should be excluded from the scheme. At the same time, it called for priority to be given to women from financially weaker sections.

The move is notable as it is the first reported instance of a civic body controlled by a UDF constituent calling for a review of the new UDF government’s much-publicised Priyadarshini scheme.

The resolution also highlighted the concerns raised by private bus owners and workers over the impact of the scheme on the sector.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 16 LIVE: Govt is ready to discuss students' protest issue; don't run away, says Rijiju amidst heavy sloganeering
World.content:
Both Houses saw couple of disruptions on Monday (August 10, 2026), Lok Sabha was adjourned minutes after the proceedings began at 11 a.m., amid protests from the Opposition demanding discussions on various issues. Rajya Sabha was also adjourned a few minutes later. Both Houses reconvened at 12 p.m. Lok Sabha introduced four Bills amid protests- The Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026, the Minerals and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 and The National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Rajya Sabha briefly took up some business, but was adjourned minutes later.

Floor leaders of the Opposition parties held a meeting in the chamber of the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, to chalk out the strategy for the Floor of the House on Monday (August 10, 2026).

The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 is also expected to be taken up in the discussion of the Opposition leaders. The Lok Sabha is scheduled to take up the introduction of several key bills on Monday, including the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, and the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

World.content:
Thousands of job aspirants, protesting against irregularities in various recruitment examinations in Jharkhand, joined the march to the State assembly on Monday (August 10, 2026). Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a hunger strike for nine days in protest against exam irregularities, also joined the march, despite losing 10.5 kg. He was seen carrying a portrait of former Jharkhand Chief Minister Shibu Soren.

The Jharkhand government on Sunday (August 9, 2026) agreed to cancel the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination and the JPSC backlog examinations held in 2023 and 2025 following six hours of discussions with protesting student groups. However, the students remained firm on their demand for a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities in the JSSC-CGL examination and said the agitation would continue. The announcement came even as all three JPSC members resigned and Chief Minister Hemant Soren assured protesters that “justice will be delivered with full transparency”.

World.title: Kerala cashew import scam: R. Chandrasekharan, K.A. Ratheesh move HC Division Bench against Single Judge order in contempt plea
World.content:
R. Chandrasekharan, INTUC Kerala State president and former chairman of Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation (KSCDC), and K.A. Ratheesh, former managing director, have filed appeals before the Division Bench of the Kerala High Court against the observations made by a Single Judge against them in a contempt of court petition in connection with the alleged irregularities in the alleged raw cashew import scam.

Mr. Chandrasekharan and Mr. Ratheesh have contended that the Single Bench, which considered the contempt plea, ignored their right to challenge the sanction order to prosecute them in the alleged misappropriation.

The CBI had sought sanction to prosecute Mr. Chandrasekharan and Mr. Ratheesh, who had held key positions in the corporation, during the period in which the alleged scam took place. The State had earlier refused the sanction thrice.

However, the State government issued the sanction order after being pulled up by the Single Judge.

The court is likely to consider the matter on Monday (August 10, 2026).

World.title: More than half of the 15,539 job-seekers either get selected or short-listed at Alva’s Pragati
World.content:
The two-day 16th edition of the mega placement drive Alva’s Pragati 2026 organised by Alva’s Education Foundation saw 285 companies select 2,394 candidates and shortlist 5,935 for further rounds of recruitment when it concluded on Saturday (August 8, 2026) in Moodbidri.
